The request's status after the decision, `skipped` for a step that
asks for a step-up or a signature, or `failed`.

BulkEditPreview.description: B5-T2: what a bulk edit would do, without doing it.

matched.description: Records picked that the caller can read.

samples.description: The first 20 records the edit would change, before and after.

unchanged.description: Picked records already holding the requested values.

BulkEditRequest.description: What to change on the picked records.

filters.description:
The records to change, by the same filters a list uses. At most 500
may match.

ids.description: The records to change, at most 500. Give `ids` or `filters`.

operations.description: The changes, applied in order to each record.

quiet.description:
B5-T3: run the edit without automation: its changes start no flow
(nor an agent a flow runs) and notify no follower. Needs the
`records.bulk_quiet` privilege.

approval_request_id.description:
B5-T3: set when the edit is above the approval count; it runs once
that approval is given, and `id` is empty until then.

id.description:
The bulk operation applying the edit; follow it at
`/api/v1/{entity}/bulk/{id}`. Empty when no record needed a change.

matched.description: Records picked that the caller can read.

record_ids.description:
B5-T4: the records the edit changes, in the order of the bulk
operation's items, so an item's `index` names its record.

total.description: Records the edit will change.

unchanged.description: Picked records already holding the requested values.

undo.description:
B5-T3: what to send to `POST /api/v1/{entity}/bulk-edit/undo` to put
the changed records back. Kept by the caller, like a clone's undo
list.

BulkEditUndoRequest.description: B5-T3: a bulk edit to put back.

quiet.description: Put the records back without automation, as for the edit itself.

undo.description: The `undo` list the bulk edit returned.

BulkFieldMode.description:
`legacy` (0): every non-sensitive field, the behaviour before D-589.
`listed` (1): only the fields in `fields`.

BulkOperation.description: What to do to the selected records.

oneOf.description:
With `include_items`: one result per item of this page, by its index
in the request (Z14-T6's `BatchResult`): `ok` when it applied,
`problem` (`version_conflict` with the record's current version in
`detail`, or `item_failed`) when it did not, neither while it has not
run.

BulkRecordEnvelope.description:
`pub(crate)` so `bulk_graph.rs`'s pure preflight functions can operate on
the same envelope shape the HTTP layer and the worker already share,
instead of introducing a second, parallel record representation.

skip_defaults.description: A28-T3: create this record without attribute defaults.

apply_defaults.description:
A28-T3: `false` leaves empty fields empty on create instead of filling
them with their attributes' defaults. Default true.

quiet.description:
B5-T3: `true` runs the operation without automation: its changes start
no flow (nor an agent a flow runs) and notify no follower. Needs the
`records.bulk_quiet` privilege. Default false.

BulkTagFailure.description: One record a bulk tag request could not change.

BulkTagRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/tags/bulk`: add one tag to, or take one tag off,
the selected records.

oneOf.description: The tag to add (an existing one, or a name to find or create).

BulkTagResult.description: What a bulk tag request did.

Bundle.description:
A whole bundle. Component vectors are in a fixed order in the struct and
each is sorted by its logical key once [`Bundle::normalize`] has run —
which [`super::canonical::canonical_json`] always does first.

attribute_patches.description:
Additive cross-module field promotion — see [`AttributePatch`].
Always present; empty when the bundle carries no patches. Never
exported automatically, same posture as [`Bundle::record_sets`]: hand
authored, since export has no way to know which fields on an entity
this bundle doesn't own are "this vertical's".

calendars.description:
D-404 / M83 Phase 1 — business calendars, holidays embedded per
calendar (a holiday has no independent identity outside its
calendar).

format.description: Always [`BUNDLE_FORMAT`] for a bundle this binary wrote.

labels.description:
M05 Phase 1 (D-426) — deployment-scope `metadata_label`
rows. Export-only; see [`COMPONENT_METADATA_LABEL`].

name.description:
M92 Phase 1 — the bundle's own identity: a stable slug an operator
assigns when authoring a named, versioned artifact (a vertical pack,
`bundle-tool export`'s hand-corrected output — see the verticals
skill's "procedure gaps" §2). `None` for an anonymous whole-deployment
export/promotion, which is the common case `export_bundle` produces
and is not itself a "named bundle". Populated identity is what lets
the ledger answer "which bundles are installed, at which versions"
(`bundle_name`/`bundle_version` in `routes::PlanListItem`) and is what
`requires.depends_on_bundles` and `POST …/bundles/{name}/rollback`
key on.

permission_sets.description:
Q10-T5 — permission sets; their assignments are environment data and
never travel.

record_sets.description:
Phase 3 (reference data) — see [`RecordSet`]. Always present; empty
when the bundle carries no reference data.

version.description:
Paired with [`Bundle::name`] — `"MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"`, the version this
specific snapshot represents (not a floor; contrast
[`Requires::platform_version`]/[`BundleDependency::min_version`],
which are floors expressed as `">=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"`).

min_version.description:
A floor, `">=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"` (a bare `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` is read
the same way) — the same convention [`Requires::platform_version`]
uses.

name.description: The required bundle's [`Bundle::name`].

BusinessRule.description:
A rule as the admin API returns it: the row, its roles and its policies.
An expression kind carries `expression`/`target_field`/`message`; a business
rule carries `applies_to`/`roles`/`condition`/`policies`.

applies_to_nobody.description: `applies_to = roles` with no live role: the rule applies to nobody.

disabled_reason.description:
Set when a Solution 7 hook turned the rule off (`field_deleted:<f>`,
`field_retyped:<f>`); cleared when an admin turns it back on.

load_error.description:
Why the stored condition or a policy could not be decoded (possible
only by bypassing this API); the registry does not enforce such a rule.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): `platform`, `product`, `project` or `customer`.

warnings.description: Editor warnings (single-rule reads and writes; empty in lists).

BusinessRuleClient.description:
One business rule as the form evaluates it (design §5): `set_value`
policies and advanced-expression conditions stay server-only. A6-T2:
field-attached `allowed_values` policies are sent, so the form offers
only the allowed choices.

BusinessRuleOp.description:
Leaf operators (string serde). `eq … in` keep `ConditionOperator`'s
meaning; the per-type table is [`ConditionFieldKind::allows`].

BusinessRulePatch.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/admin/business-rules/{id}`: any field of
[`BusinessRuleBody`]; `entity` and `name` may be sent but not changed.

CachePurge.description: What to purge: one key (as the cache's readers name it), or everything.

key.description: The id to drop; omit it to drop every entry.

name.description: The cache, by its declared name. Filled from the path.

CacheStatsRow.description: One declared cache's numbers on one node.

entries.description: Entries in the in-process tier now.

evictions.description: Entries pushed out by the capacity or the quota.

hit_rate.description: hits / (hits + misses), or `null` before the first read.

hits.description: Reads the in-process tier answered since this node started.

misses.description: Reads that went on to the shared store or the source.

node.description: The node these numbers are from (each node counts its own).

CalculateOp.description: Z12-T10: one business-time question for a calendar.

user_id.description:
Answer on this person's calendar, with their absences, instead of
`{id}`. Only the caller themselves, or an administrator.

CalculateResponse.description: Z12-T10: the answer, and what it was computed against.

result.description:
A timestamp for `add` and `next`, minutes for `between`, a boolean
for `is_working`.

parent_calendar_id.description:
Z12-T6: the calendar this one inherits from; its chain may not loop
or run deeper than three calendars.

CalendarDef.description:
`calendar` — one named business calendar (D-404 / M83 Phase 1).
Not a generic XRM entity (same posture as `ViewDef`/`view`), so
addressed by `name` alone rather than `(entity, name)`. `working_days` is
a lowercase 3-letter weekday array (`"mon"`..`"sun"`); `hours` is
`{"mon": [{"start_minute": 540, "end_minute": 1020}], ...}`, matching
`calendar.hours`'s jsonb shape exactly (round-tripped verbatim,
not reparsed into a typed shape here — the same posture `ViewDef.
table_definition` already takes for its own opaque jsonb column).

country_code.description: Z12-T3: an ISO 3166 country code, such as `SA`.

exceptions.description:
D-592 per-date exceptions. `None` (a bundle written before they
existed) leaves the target's exceptions alone; `Some` is the exact
list, keyed by `exception_date`. Export always writes `Some`.

parent.description:
Z12-T4: the calendar this one inherits from, by name. `None` leaves
the target's parent alone.

rules.description:
Z12-T6: holiday rules by name. `None` leaves the target's alone;
`Some` is the exact list. Export writes them when there are any.

seasons.description: Z12-T6: seasonal hours by name, the same way as `rules`.

country_code.description: Z12-T3: an ISO 3166 country code, such as `SA`.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this calendar: `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer
may update or retire it (409 `layer_mismatch` otherwise).

parent.description: The parent's name (how a changeset names it).

parent_calendar_id.description: Z12-T4: the calendar this one inherits from.

CalendarExceptionDef.description:
One `calendar_exception` row (D-592), embedded under its
calendar and identified by `exception_date` within it.

ranges.description: `[{"start_minute", "end_minute"}]` on that local date; `[]` closes it.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this exception row (it may
differ from its calendar's). Only a changeset of that layer may
remove it.

ranges.description:
Empty: the date is closed. Otherwise these ranges replace the
weekday's hours for that date.

last_error.description: Why the last fetch failed: an HTTP status or a parse failure.

CalendarFeedBody.description: A feed as an administrator adds it.

url.description: An `https` URL whose host resolves to a public address.

CalendarFull.description: Z12-T6: one calendar with its holiday rules and seasons.

CalendarTimeRange.description: One working range on an exception's date, minutes from local midnight.

activity_id.description: The `phone_call` activity logged for it; the outcome is recorded on it.

CancelTransitionBody.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/transition/cancel` — withdraws the record's
open transition approval (requester only) and returns the record to the
state it came from; or, when that approval was already closed without
executing (rejected, expired, invalidated) but the record is still
parked, finishes returning it (the requester or an administrator).

comment.description: Recorded on the audit events. Optional.

CancelTurnView.description: What a Stop request found (C11 B4).

slack_minutes.description:
Minutes between arrival (now plus travel) and the job's due time;
negative when late.

travel_minutes.description: Minutes to the site, when both points are known.

CapabilityPackRef.description:
One pack that contributed to a session's allowed-action set, with the
`row_version` it held at the moment the session started.

The id alone is not enough: packs are versioned, so "which capabilities did
this session hold" must be answerable later without depending on what the
pack says now (D-556 §2). This is the same `{ref, row_version}` pair
`PolicySnapshot::policy_ref`/`policy_row_version` already carries.

CapacityRow.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/resources/capacity` — a single resource's
capacity/demand picture over the requested `[from, to]` period (M72).
See `capacity.rs`'s module doc for the exact arithmetic behind each
field — in short: `capacity_hours` is the platform's default business
calendar over the period, net of approved leave; `allocated_hours` is
`resource_allocation.allocation_percent` prorated by date overlap;
`actual_hours` is `project_time_entry.hours`, unrelated to either.

actual_hours.description:
`SUM(hours)` from `project_time_entry` for this resource, entries
dated within `[from, to]` — what was actually logged, independent of
what was planned.

allocated_hours.description:
`SUM(allocation_percent / 100 * capacity_hours * overlap_days /
period_days)` across every `resource_allocation` row overlapping
the period — prorated against the period's nominal (pre-leave)
capacity, not the leave-adjusted figure above; see `capacity.rs`.

capacity_hours.description:
Business-calendar working hours over `[from, to]`, net of any
`resource_availability` leave overlapping the period.

over_allocated.description:
`allocated_hours > capacity_hours` — the resource is committed past
what the period's business calendar (net of leave) can deliver.

resource_name.description:
`user_account.user_name` — `None` for a legacy row with no
username set, same optionality the column itself carries.

utilization_pct.description:
`allocated_hours / capacity_hours * 100`; `0.0` when `capacity_hours`
is `0` (e.g. a period with no working days at all, or a resource on
leave for the whole period) rather than a division-by-zero `NaN`.

label.description:
A human name for this snapshot (e.g. "Sprint 3 baseline"). Capturing
twice with the same label for the same project is safe — see this
module's doc comment — and returns the existing baseline rather than
creating a duplicate.

item_count.description:
Number of `project_baseline_item` rows captured under this
baseline — every active work item on the project at capture time.

channel.description: E27-T3: the channel consented to; `email` when unset.

country.description:
E27-T3: the person's country (ISO code), for the double opt-in
rule; the deployment's own country when unset.

CaptureOutcome.description: What became of a captured grant.

version_no.description: The suite's draft after the case was added.

activity_mapping.description:
Interpretation depends on `source` — see `extraction.rs`'s doc
comment for the exact shape each source kind expects.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this definition.

visibility_privilege.description:
M41 §5 Permissions — a privilege key aggregate DFG/variant views will
require of the caller. Stored and schema-ready; enforcing it on a
self-service (non-admin) read surface is Phase 2+ (Phase 1 exposes
only the admin-gated routes this crate mounts today).

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this definition —
`platform`, `product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of
that layer may change or retire it.

message_id.description: The assistant message that went wrong.

name.description: The case's name; defaults to one naming the message.

role_id.description: The role to grant; the one asked for when omitted.

CatalogAccessRequest.description: A request for access to an asset.

approval_request_id.description: When the grant waits for a second administrator (D-195).

role_ref.description: The role asked for or granted.

role_id.description: The role that would give the access, when the requester knows it.

CatalogAssetPage.description:
Everything known about one asset, each fact from the feature that owns
it; a fact whose feature this deployment lacks (its table is absent) is
`null`, not an error.

domain.description: The data domain (M15): id, name, description, steward.

lineage.description: What reads the entity (or the attribute): queries, flows, dashboards, rules.

profile.description:
The latest completed profile of the entity (an attribute's own
column only, for an attribute).

quality.description: The latest quality score per dimension of the asset's entity.

terms.description: Glossary terms of the asset's entity.

CatalogAssetSearch.description: A page of assets with the facet counts.

CatalogAssetSummary.description: One asset as the catalogue lists it.

description_status.description:
`missing`, `draft` (proposed, by a person or an agent) or `reviewed`
(approved by a builder).

ref.description: The asset's own reference: a logical name, `entity.field` or an id.

CatalogExportAsset.description: One asset as the export lists it: metadata only, never record values.

CatalogFacet.description: One facet value and its count.

CatalogFacets.description: Counts by kind, domain and label over the visible assets the query matches.

hidden.description:
L4-T3: listed by name only because the caller may not read it (only
when the deployment shows hidden attributes; ask for access).

to_attribute.description: `None` for an entity-level reference (0356's empty-string sentinel).

unused.description: L4-T5: no write in 90 days, no search in 30 and no reader.

new_total.description: The order's new total, as a decimal string.

ChangeFeedEntry.description:
One row of the unified feed. `reference` is always the id of the actual
source record (not this feed's own bookkeeping), so a caller can follow up
against that source's own admin surface.

actor.description:
Best-effort — `None` when the source records no actor at all (see the
module doc's per-source notes), never fabricated.

ChangeKind.description:
One source this feed aggregates. The wire value (`kind` filter and each
entry's own `kind` field) is this variant's snake_case name.

approval_pending.description:
`true` when this call only submitted a pending four-eyes approval
request rather than deciding the change request immediately —
mirrors `attome-dashboard::lifecycle::PublishResponse`'s own field.

client_ref.description: The S2S client (`s2s_client.id`) that reads it.

service_user_ref.description: The client's service user, as whom every event is filtered.

field_type.description: `text | number | currency | date | bool | choice | rich_text`.

ChangedAttribute.description: M9-T4: one attribute a request would change.

from.description: The value when the request was opened.

cursor.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous call; absent to start from now.

has_more.description: Whether the page was full: more changes may be waiting.

removed.description: Records deleted since the cursor, or no longer visible to the caller.

upserted.description: Records added or changed since the cursor that the caller may read.

ChangesetOperation.description:
One recorded operation as the review sees it (the raw row snapshot stays
server-side; `args` is set once the changeset is closed).

object_ref.description: The live row, for diagnostics; never exported.

apply_ids.description:
Every planned expand row, in apply order — what `apply` takes for
`phase = expand`.

contract_apply_ids.description: Every contract row, in apply order.

ChangesetSummary.description: A changeset without its document or operations.

checksum.description: Set once the changeset is closed (an automatic one: once sealed).

row_version.description: Send as `If-Match` to close or abandon.

ChannelRow.description: A channel as its member sees it.

unread.description: Messages from others since the caller last marked the channel read.

ChartCompany.description: A company in a group chart.

citations.description:
C11 B6 (row A-86): on an assistant answer grounded in the widget's
knowledge, the sources it drew on — title and section only. Omitted
when there are none, so a widget that predates it receives exactly the
response it always did. Not stored: a later poll returns the message
without them.

direction.description: `inbound` (the visitor) or `outbound` (the bot, or a human agent).

note.description: Why it is checked out, shown to others (at most 500 characters).

method.description: The method the payer chose; card by default.

redirect_url.description: Send the payer here (a hosted page)...

ChildSession.description: One session a supervisor delegated to (N8-T1's run tree).

agent_object_ref.description: The specialist agent object it ran as.

counted.description:
`false` on a table too large to count inline; `values` then lists the
choices with no counts.

ChoiceValueUsage.description: One value of a choice field and the records holding it.

defined.description:
The value is one of the field's current choices; `false` for a value
still stored after it was removed.

CitationView.description:
One citation, projected from `attome_search::KnowledgeCitation` — every field
except `passage`, whose text is already in the turn's tool message. An
explicit shape, never the stored JSON passed through.

data_source_id.description: The Data Source that permissioned it at retrieval time.

fetched_at.description: When a web-sourced passage was fetched; `null` for authored articles.

heading_path.description: The heading path of the cited section, outermost first.

item_id.description: The knowledge article the passage came from.

stale.description: Past its `review_by` date when it was retrieved.

truncated.description: The section was returned in part.

claimed.description:
`false` when the queue is currently empty — not an error, just
nothing to claim right now.

oneOf.description: `None` when no callable member is left.

Cleanup.description: What needs tidying in the graph.

cycles.description: Definitions that, through other definitions, depend on themselves.

dangling.description: Edges to an entity or attribute that no longer exists.

unused_attributes.description: Active attributes no definition uses, as `entity.attribute`.

CleanupItem.description: One record in a rule's clean-up queue.

owner_ref.description: The record's owner, who is asked to fix it.

note.description: Why the hold no longer applies (1 to 500 characters).

can_act_as_user.description: S1-T10: may name a user to act as.

oauth_public_key_set.description: S11-T1: whether a public key for token-endpoint assertions is set.

oauth_scopes.description: S11-T1: the scopes an access token may carry.

owner_user_ref.description: S11-T4: the person answerable for the client.

methods.description:
S11-T6: how the client can authenticate: `key` (an active HMAC key,
whose secret also serves `client_secret_basic`), `public_key` (a JWT
signed by its key, S11-T1) and `identity_provider` (a trusted
identity provider's token, S11-T2).

owner_user_ref.description: S11-T4: the person answerable for the client, and their address.

CloneChild.description:
A child relationship: records of `entity` whose `field` points at the
record being copied.

children.description: Child records to copy with it, by relationship.

overrides.description: Values for the copy that replace the source's, by field.

preview.description: Return the copy's body without creating it.

CloneResult.description: What a clone made, or would make.

body.description: The body sent to the create path.

children.description: The child relationships copied with it.

id.description: The new record's id; absent for a preview.

left_out.description: Fields of the source left out of the copy, and why.

undo.description:
Every record made, children first, at the version it was made with:
the body of `POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/clone/undo`. Empty for a
preview.

CloneUndoItem.description: One record a clone made, at the version the clone left it.

operation_id.description:
Their delete operation:
`POST /api/v1/bin/operations/{operation_id}/restore` brings them back.

removed.description: Records moved to the recycle bin.

ClonedChildren.description: What a clone did with one child relationship.

count.description: Child records found and readable (copied, or that would be).

ids.description: The copies' ids; empty for a preview.

skipped.description: Child records the caller cannot read, left behind.

changeset.description:
The `attome-changeset/v1` document; write it into the repository with
`node scripts/changesets/write-closed.mjs --dir <folder>`.

summary.description:
Plain-language review text (the same wording as
`scripts/changesets/summarize.mjs`).

kind.description:
`non_portable_value` (translation left a deployment-local id out) or
`unrecorded_entity_change` (the metadata change log shows the entity
changed after the changeset opened, and no recorded operation covers
it).

lag_bytes.description: Bytes behind the leader, when Patroni knows.

chunks_embedded.description:
Chunks carrying a vector from the configured model. `None` when
knowledge is lexical-only by configuration.

embedding_backlog.description:
Chunks still waiting for a vector from the configured model (never
embedded, or embedded by a different one). `None` when knowledge is
lexical-only by configuration.

items_draft.description: Items waiting in the draft review queue. Never chunked (D-489).

items_total.description: Live items in the collection, whatever their lifecycle.

last_indexed_at.description: The newest `indexed_at` among those chunks; `None` when there are none.

choice_styles.description:
Per-value color/icon presentation hints for a `data_type: "choice"`
column — the raw `choice_styles` map from `attome_field::ChoiceOptions`,
keyed by choice value. `None` for every other column, and for a
choice column with no configured styles. Metadata-derived, set
alongside `data_type` in the enrichment loop below.

lookup_target_entity.description:
Logical name of the entity a `data_type: "lookup"` column points to —
`None` for every other column. Metadata-derived (never from
`table_definition`), set alongside `data_type` in the enrichment loop
below. The frontend turns this into a route
(`logicalToUrlPath`) to make an unconfigured lookup cell clickable by
default — a plain logical name, not a route, so this crate stays free
of Angular's routing scheme.

contract_ids.description: Two or more contracts of one customer; the first is kept.

base_hash.description:
The content hash of the document the commands were made against; empty
for an object that does not exist yet.

name.description: The object's name; required when it does not exist yet.

issues.description: References to objects that do not exist; they do not block the draft.

amount.description: Decimal text; negative takes pay away.

CommissionAdjustmentOutcome.description: The adjustment written, or the approval it waits on.

approval_request_id.description: The approval request, when the amount is above the threshold.

CommissionDisputeDecision.description: A reviewer's decision on a dispute.

amount.description: Required for `adjust`: the adjustment, as decimal text.

CommissionEstimate.description: What one opportunity would pay if it closed now.

payout.description: The opportunity's own payout across the plan's components.

period_change.description:
How the period's total changes with it (more than `payout` when it
lifts every credit into a higher retroactive band).

run_ids.description: One calculation run per plan version.

amount.description: Absent when the caller may not see pay amounts.

explanation.description: A line's explanation steps; an adjustment's reason.

Comparator.description: How one field of a rule compares two records.

CompareMetricColumn.description:
`pub` (this struct and the three below, fields too) — `do_compare`
returns this directly and this crate's own `tests/scenario.rs` inspects
it, same reasoning as `ScenarioResultRow` above.

cells.description:
Aligned by index with the response's `metrics` array — a `null`-shaped
entry (`status = "not_evaluated"`) stands in for a metric this
scenario references but has never run `evaluate` for.

Comparison.description: The edges added and removed between two versions.

ComparisonReport.description: The whole report: every group matching the filter, plus when it was run.

ComparisonRow.description:
One `(action, model_id, prompt_version)` group's outcome rates, each with
its own Wilson interval sized to that group's own sample.

total_decided.description:
Non-pending outcomes — the denominator every rate below is computed
against. Excludes `pending` for the same reason `quality_monitor.rs`
and `compliance_report.rs` do: an undecided suggestion is neither a
success nor a failure yet.

article.description:
The knowledge article holding the battle card, when one is set, the
deployment names its article entity and the caller may read it.

competitor.description:
The competitor's fields the caller may read (name, strengths,
weaknesses, price position, regions, battle card id).

acceptance_rate.description:
`(accepted + edited) / (accepted + edited + rejected)`. `None` when
there are zero decided outcomes for this model — a rate of "0%" would
misreport "everyone rejected it" when really nobody has decided yet.

approved.description:
`true` when a live `ai_model` catalog row names this model with
`approval_status = 'approved'`.
**`in_use && !approved` is the finding this report exists to catch.**

in_use.description:
`true` when this model has at least one row in
`ai_suggestion_outcome` — it was actually invoked.

outcomes_without_provenance.description:
Governance-sensitive count of `ai_suggestion_outcome` rows missing
model_id/prompt_version/action_id — see this module's doc comment for
why this should always read zero and how it is nonetheless checked as
data rather than assumed from the schema.

attachments.description:
J1-T2: the record's own files to send with an email, by file key (at
most 10, 10 MiB together).

channel.description:
`email` or `internal` — Phase 1 accepts no other value (see this
module's doc comment).

recipient_user_ids.description:
Recipient `user_account` ids. Required, non-empty, for
`channel=internal`; ignored otherwise.

send_at.description:
J1-T1: send no earlier than this (email only, up to 90 days ahead).
The author's signature is appended to an email either way.

to.description:
Recipient email addresses. Required, non-empty, for `channel=email`;
ignored otherwise.

id.description: The record, for update and delete; may be a `${ref.id}` reference.

ref.description:
This operation's name, for later references: lowercase letters,
digits and `_`, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters.

all_or_none.description: Every operation commits or none does. Not available yet (S1-T8).

error.description: The error body, as a single request would have answered.

status.description: The HTTP status the operation would have had on its own.

actual.description:
Required when the metric is `source_kind = "manual"`; ignored for
`"query"`.

force.description:
When `true`, always writes a new snapshot — D-407's restatement path
— chained via `superseded_ref` to whatever was there before, which is
left untouched.

period_start.description:
Defaults to the metric's current period (today's day/week/month/
quarter/year boundary, UTC).

skipped.description:
`true` when an existing snapshot was returned unchanged (idempotent
skip) rather than a new one being computed.

ComputeTreeResponse.description: A tree computation, in the order it ran.

all.description:
The tree nests, so utoipa must not expand it inline (the recursion
would overflow the stack while building the OpenAPI document).

expression.description:
A `attome-rules` expression over the entity's own fields that types as
`bool`. A rule with an advanced leaf may not carry `hidden` or
`disabled` policies (the client cannot mirror it).

value.description: A literal (an array for `in`). Exactly one of `value` and `value_ref`.

value_ref.description:
`@portal_user.id`, or `@portal_user.<lookup field>` (e.g.
`@portal_user.account_ref`). Only with `eq`. Resolved per request; a
null or missing value matches no row.

`field` may be `id`, the record's own key, with `eq` only: that is how
a role reaches the portal user's own parent record
(`id = @portal_user.company_ref`).

ConditionTree.description:
A condition: `{"all": [...]}` (AND), `{"any": [...]}` (OR), a structured
leaf `{"field", "op", "value"?}`, or an advanced leaf `{"expression"}`
holding a `attome-rules` boolean. The root `{"all": []}` means "always".

ConfidenceInterval.description: A Wilson score confidence interval, `[lower, upper] ⊆ [0, 1]`.

ConfigChange.description: One changed key in a comparison.

ConfiguredAccess.description:
The "configured" half: every raw assignment that feeds resolution, with
display names attached so the UI doesn't need N follow-up lookups.

ConfirmApprovalRequested.description: `202`: a `Consequential` action was submitted for four-eyes approval.

ConfirmConflict.description:
A confirm or reject that did not run anything: the standard error body
(`error` is always `"conflict"` or `"rate_limit_exceeded"`) plus the
outcome decided from the persisted state.

approval_request_id.description: `approval_pending`: the approval request it waits on.

result.description: `already_executed`: the recorded result of the execution that ran.

token.description: The signed token from the link.

ConfirmToolCallRequest.description:
Body of `POST …/tool-calls/{tid}/confirm`. **Only the hash the UI
displayed** — the arguments that run are the server's stored copy (I-13).
An `arguments` field, or any other, is rejected (row A-08).

ConflictCount.description: A16-T7: the conflicts of the last `days` days, by entity and source.

oneOf.description:
E27-T3: what became of a captured grant in the consent ledger, when
the form named a contact, lead or account.

accepted.description:
The signed-in user has accepted the current versions (always true when
the portal requires none).

ConsumerHealth.description: L7-T7: how one change-feed consumer is keeping up.

lag_events.description: Events written after its cursor, up to [`LAG_COUNT_CAP`].

lag_seconds.description: Age of its oldest unread event; 0 when it has read everything.

last_event_at.description: The time of the last event it read, if any.

last_read_at.description: When it last advanced its cursor.

status.description: `active`, or `expired` once it fell past its allowed lag.

events.description: All events kept for the contact.

last_seen_at.description: The latest event of any kind.

total_purchases.description: The sum of purchase events' numeric `amount`.

ContentSpace.description:
A reusable container of pages — a pure organizational grouping, not a URL
namespace (`url_path` uniqueness stays global across all spaces; see
D-369). Infra-mutable class (D-005).

blog_path.description: Pages under this path are the site's blog posts.

domain.description: E12-T2: the domain this space is served on.

kind.description: E11-T1: `standard` or `marketing` (landing pages), set at create.

require_approval.description: K5-T1: a publish in this space waits for approval.

ContrastFailure.description: One pair that reads too faintly, or two status colours too alike.

ratio.description: The measured contrast ratio, or ΔE for `distinct`.

ControlBody.description: A control request: the instance's current `row_version`.

ControlResult.description: The instance's state after a control action.

last_ordinal.description: The ordinal of the last message; the history's `total`.

from_type.description:
The type the caller expects the field to have now; `type_drift` when
it differs. Omitted = the live type.

map.description:
text -> choice: source text -> choice value (the values become the
field's choices).

organization_id.description:
The organization the new project is created under — required because
`organization_id` is a required lookup on `attome_project` and nothing on
`service_work_request` names one.

project_id.description:
The project the new task (`project_work_item`) is created under —
required because `project_id` is a required lookup on that entity and
nothing on `service_work_request` names one.

map_ids.description: The maps to convert with, in order; more than one splits the request.

values.description:
Values for the target records that the request cannot supply (a
required parent, say), applied over every map's result.

ConvertWithMapsResponse.description: What a conversion with maps created.

CookedRef.description: One artefact of the current version.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the artefact's bytes, lowercase hex.

CoverageImpact.description: What a person's absence does to coverage.

expires_in_days.description:
P-account-lifecycle — overrides `auth.apikey_default_expiry_days` for
this one key. `None` (the default when the field is omitted) falls
back to the configured default, itself `None` unless an operator set
it — so an old client that never sends this field keeps getting
no-expiry keys exactly as before, unless the deployment opted in.

ends_at.description: When the assignment stops giving anything; open-ended when omitted.

error.description: Why it would not, as the create would say it.

failures.description: A3-T1: every failing field, when the create failed on its fields.

warnings.description: Business-rule warnings the create would raise.

can_act_as_user.description: S1-T10: the client may name a user to act as (`x-attome-act-as`).

client_id.description: Machine-readable slug, e.g. "sap-erp". Immutable after creation.

expires_at.description:
S11-T4: when the client stops working; its owner is reminded 14 days
before.

owner_user_ref.description: S11-T4: the person answerable for the client; the caller by default.

purpose.description: S11-T4: what the client is for.

service_user_ref.description:
The `user_account` this client acts as: every S2S-authenticated
request runs with that user's privileges and is attributed to it in
the audit trail. S11-T4: omit it and the client gets a service user
of its own with no role, so it can do nothing until granted one.

reason.description: Why the pair conflicts; shown to whoever is refused or asked.

kind.description:
D17-T1: `flow` (the default), `journey`, `nurture` or `sequence`.
Fixed once created.

pages.description:
Same shape `pages_snapshot` produces — every `id` may be omitted, a
fresh one is always generated (`IdPolicy::GenerateNewIds`).

answers.description: Answers to the template's prompts, by field name.

register_link.description:
The fully-qualified register link — handed to an admin to relay to the
invitee directly, since `config.email.enabled = false` (no SMTP
configured) is a fully supported deployment shape (D-002 single-tenant
air-gapped install). Also emailed when `email.enabled` is true, same
dual-path pattern as `register`'s own verification-email step.

CreateInvitationResponse.description:
Only ever returned once, right after minting — same "the caller needs the
actual bearer at least once" reasoning as every other token-issuance
response in this codebase (e.g. MFA's one-time recovery-code batch). Never
re-derivable from `list_invitations`, which only ever returns
`InvitationItem` (no `bearer`/`register_link` field).

scan_schedule.description: A15-T6: `hourly`, `daily` or `weekly` full scans; absent: on demand.

CreateModelBody.description:
`POST /api/v1/admin/predict/models` body. No `features`/`algorithm` field:
Phase 1 has no per-model configurable feature set yet — `features` is
derived and overwritten from `features::FEATURE_KEYS` once training
actually runs (`model::FeatureDescriptor`'s own doc comment), and
`algorithm` is always `logistic_regression` — so accepting either here
would just be a client-supplied value this crate silently ignores.

template_id.description:
When set, must be one of `content_space_id`'s allowed templates
(`content_space_template`) — its `blocks` are copied into the new
page's `blocks_draft` once, at create time.

entity.description:
Entity logicalname (matches `AvailableViewsQuery.entity` — the shape a
self-service caller already has, unlike the admin `ViewBody`'s
`entity_logical_name: Uuid`, which requires resolving the entity's id
first; that resolution happens server-side here instead).

owner.description: Defaults to the caller when omitted.

format.description:
`csv`, `xlsx` or `pptx` (P4-T1) — anything else is rejected by the
`format` attribute's `choice` options (see module doc).

parameters.description:
Default parameter filters applied when a run doesn't override them —
same `Filter` grammar `query/execute` and `{entity}/export` already
use, so no new binding/whitelisting surface is introduced.

ip_allowlist.description:
Every entry is validated (`attome_server::middleware::ip_allowlist::
validate_cidr_list`) before the write — a typo'd CIDR is rejected here
at save time rather than silently never matching at request time.

position_hierarchy_enabled.description:
Defaults to `false` — the DB column default (migration 0053); a role
created without specifying this never extends via position hierarchy.

expression.description: A condition each record must hold, e.g. `amount >= 0`.

staged_import_id.description:
An `automation_staged_import` id already created via
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/staged-import` (with this project's
`mapping_ref`, and `mode: "dry_run"` for a preview run).

recipients.description:
User emails, team names, or literal email addresses — resolved at
delivery time, not validated against a directory here (same
"opaque until delivery" posture `record_share`'s
principal resolution uses for `user_email`/`team_name`).

expires_in_hours.description: Hours until the link stops working, 1 to 720 (30 days); 72 when absent.

key.description:
For a multi-file field, which stored object to share (one of the
field's keys); ignored for a single-file field.

max_downloads.description: Optional limit on downloads, at least 1.

password.description:
Optional; whoever opens the link must give it. The same strength
rules as an account password apply.

kind.description:
E11-T1: `standard` (the default) or `marketing`; a marketing space
starts with the landing page templates. Fixed once created.

require_approval.description: K5-T1: a publish in this space waits for approval.

locked_states.description: M8-T2: states in which a record is read-only except the listed fields.

reason_field.description: M8-T2: an attribute of the entity holding the status reason.

reasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons each state allows; a state listed here needs one.

record_type.description:
M8-T2: the record type (a `record_type` code of the entity) this model
governs; omit for the entity's model of every other record. Fixed once
created. A typed model is not recorded in changesets or bundles: make
it through this API in each deployment.

state_field.description: Must name an existing `Choice` attribute on `entity_logicalname`.

external_system.description:
L1-T7: the system this subscriber is, as master-data contributions
name it; a golden-record change then carries its own external id.

filter_event_names.description:
Matches a named change-feed event (`attome_core::change_feed::
emit_named`, e.g. `"sla.breached"`) — migration `0441`,
REVIEW-2026-09-02 finding #3. An unnamed (ordinary) event never
matches a non-null list here.

filter_expression.description:
Reserved for M45 (attome-rules) — stored, never evaluated in Phase 1.
See `attome_events::filter`'s module doc.

ordered.description: M13-T3: send one record's events one at a time, in order.

payload_shape.description:
M13-T1: `id`, `changes` or `full` (the default): what each webhook
body carries besides the entity, record id and operation.

target_auth_header.description:
M13-T2: a header the target wants on every delivery, e.g.
`Authorization`; its value is write-only.

config.description:
L1-T3: for `source_system_rank`, `{"ranks": {"<attribute>" | "*":
["<system>", ...]}, "tie_break": "recency" | "completeness",
"validated_only": bool}`; absent for the other strategies.

JSON-encoded adapter config (endpoint templates, pagination style) —
stored as-is; `connector::adapters::rest` reads it once Phase 2 needs
per-system endpoint shaping.

credential_value.description:
Plaintext, accepted exactly once — never stored on the entity row,
never echoed back. Optional: a system can be registered before its
credential is known and rotated in later.

service_principal_ref.description:
The `user_account` id whose `SecurityContext` gates every
write this system's inbound webhook makes (D-425) — see
`system::ensure_service_principal_exists`.

include_patterns.description:
K6-T1 source settings; each one omitted keeps its default (or, on a
re-submitted URL, the value the target already has).

max_depth.description:
Defaults to `config.webcrawl.max_depth` (6) when omitted; clamped to
`MIN_DEPTH..=MAX_DEPTH` regardless of what's requested.

oneOf.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): an approval plan (ordered `any`/`all`/`n_of_m`
steps of `user:`/`role:`/`team:`/`position:manager_of_requester`
tokens), validated with attome-approval's own validator. Requires
`pending_state`.

auto_condition.description:
M8-T3: an attome-rules condition over the record's fields (such as
`due_date < today()`). When it holds for a record in `from_state`,
the transition happens by itself, checked after each write and daily.

on_reject_state.description:
An option of the state field; defaults to `from_state`. Only allowed
with `approval_plan`.

pending_state.description:
An option of the model's state field, other than `from_state`,
`to_state` and the model's initial state. Required with, and only
allowed with, `approval_plan`.

language.description: The translation's language code, e.g. `ar` or `en-GB`.

audience.description: The audience its tokens must carry for this deployment.

channel.description:
G2-T1: the `channel` choice the request came through (`portal` for
an anonymous web form); unset leaves it empty.

request_type.description:
`project_request | change_request | issue_report | it_request |
hr_request | access_request | custom` — the same `service_work_request
.request_type` choice set. Not derived from the offering: an offering
can plausibly back more than one request type, so the caller states
it explicitly, the same "don't guess a product decision" reasoning
`convert.rs`'s required parent lookups already apply.

requester_id.description:
The `user_account` this request is filed on behalf of — the
caller's choice, made explicit, same reasoning as `convert.rs`'s
`project_id`/`organization_id` fields.

converted.description:
G2-T3: the records the request became at once, through the
offering's direct-creation conversion maps; empty when it has none
(or the conversion could not be made, which leaves the request to
convert by hand).

open_requests.description:
G2-T2: the requester's other open requests, newest first, so the
submission can be added to one instead. Empty when the caller may not
read work requests.

portal_token.description:
The self-service portal bearer token (`{public_id}.{secret}`) —
returned exactly once, here. Only its argon2 hash is persisted
(`service_work_request.portal_secret_hash`); this response is the only
place the raw secret ever exists.

reference.description:
G2-T2: the request's reference (`REQ-2026-00042`), when the
deployment's reference rule numbered it.

children.description: The child records created with it.

CreatedShareLink.description: A new link. `token` and `path` are shown this once.

path.description: The public path to hand out: `/api/v1/shared-files/{token}`.

CreditApplied.description:
What applying an account's unapplied credit did: one entry per payment
whose credit paid something.

currency.description: The open invoices' currency; none when there are none.

limit.description: The account's limit; none means no limit.

open_balance.description: What the account owes on its open invoices.

CreditLine.description: One original line to credit, and how much of it.

quantity.description: A positive quantity, at most what is still uncredited on the line.

CurrencyStatement.description: A statement's section in one currency.

CurrentConflict.description: One person holding both sides of a rule now.

One run behind a number: an outcome row (`tasks`, `handoffs`) or a

only); absent otherwise.

The optimistic-concurrency version the item's `actions` routes expect
back, when they take one — for an approval that is the approval
request's current `row_version`, which `POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/
decide` requires. Omitted (`None`) by every provider whose actions

The owning entity's logical name, for a client that wants to link to
the record or run its own further checks.

ErrorCode.description:
Every `error` code the API answers with.

`not_found`: No such resource, or the caller may not see it.
`unauthorized`: Missing or invalid credentials.
`forbidden`: The caller lacks the privilege for this action.
`attribute_not_writable`: The write sets an attribute the caller may not write; `field` names it.
`limit_exceeded`: The request is past a limit; `limit`, `value` and `next` say which and what to do.
`conflict`: The request conflicts with the current state.
`version_conflict`: The record changed since the caller read it; read it again and retry.
`duplicate_detected`: The save matches existing records under a blocking duplicate rule.
`idempotency_conflict`: The idempotency key was used for a different request.
`validation_error`: The request failed validation.
`customer_tests_failed`: A publish was refused because blocking customer tests failed; `tests` names them.
`rule_violation`: A business rule refused the write; `rule_id` names it.
`field_locked`: A business rule locks a field the write changed.
`field_locked_required`: A locked field is required and was left empty.
`feature_unavailable`: The feature is not available on this deployment.
`feature_hidden`: The feature is switched off for this deployment.
`rate_limit_exceeded` (retryable): Too many requests; wait for `Retry-After`.
`overloaded` (retryable): The server is overloaded; retry shortly.
`capability_unavailable` (retryable): A service the request needs is down; retry after `Retry-After`.
`metadata_authoring_locked`: Metadata changes are locked on this deployment.
`transition_not_allowed`: The state model does not allow this change of state.
`reauth_required`: The action needs a fresh sign-in or second factor first.
`server_timeout` (retryable): The request took too long; it may be retried.
`query_timeout`: An interactive query ran past its limit; run it as an export.
`read_only` (retryable): Changes are paused on this deployment; reads still work.
`payload_too_large`: The request body is too large or too deeply nested.
`request_rejected`: The request was refused before it reached a route: a malformed path or oversized headers.
`invalid_cursor`: The cursor was not issued by this deployment; start again from the first page.
`resync_needed`: The delta token is older than the change feed keeps; read the list again for a new token.
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`: An earlier attempt with this key did not finish; its outcome is unknown.
`idempotency_replay_unavailable`: The stored response for this key can no longer be replayed.
`method_not_allowed`: The path exists but not for this method; see `Allow`.
`api_version_sunset`: The API version this request is answered at was retired; `supported` lists the current ones.
`unsupported_api_version`: The `Attome-Version` header names a version this server does not answer; `supported` lists the ones it does.
`internal_error` (retryable): An unexpected error; the request id finds it in the logs.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

extra.description: What a kind records beyond these fields.

rpo_seconds.description: Data lost, measured: the recovery point.

rto_seconds.description: Time to serve again, measured: the recovery time.

EvidencePack.description: Events, their proofs, the public keys and how to check them offline.

EvidencePackRequest.description: What an evidence pack covers: a time range, or one record.

created.description: False when this evidence was already stored.

outcome.description: The action's outcome, or what a person did with a suggestion.

expires_at.description: When the exception ends once approved; none for no end.

target_ref.description:
What the exception covers (an entity, an `entity.attribute`, a
record id, ...).

next_cursor.description:
Present only in cursor mode: the `after_id` value the caller passes
back to fetch the next page. `None` means either OFFSET mode, or
cursor mode with no further rows (the page came back short).

total.description:
`None` in keyset/cursor mode (P1.11(g)) — `COUNT(*) OVER()` scans the
full matching set regardless of OFFSET vs keyset, a cost independent
of (and additional to) the O(offset) problem keyset fixes, so cursor
requests skip it rather than pay for a total the typical cursor
caller (export/infinite-scroll/API integration) doesn't need.

total_estimated.description:
A13-T2: `true` when `total` is the planner's estimate rather than a
count: a matching set of [`EXACT_TOTAL_LIMIT`] rows or more is not
counted, as counting it would scan it all.

can_edit_query.description:
The caller may open the admin query editor for this exact query.
Query mutations are currently system.admin-only, so derive this from
the same authoritative SecurityContext that authorized execution.

entity_logical_name.description:
Logical name resolved from the query's entity UUID link. Clients use
this to derive generic list/form routes without hardcoded entity URLs.

view_id.description: Presentation view used for this execution. Raw query executions have no view.

view_kind.description:
D-429's view `kind` (chart follow-up, migration 0447) — `None` when
this execution has no bound view. Lets a non-admin client (e.g. the
dashboard widget viewer) render `kind`-specific settings without a
second, admin-gated call — see `SqlQueryRow::view_kind`'s doc comment.

after_id.description:
P1.11(g)/P-stored-query-containment phase 2: the id of the last row
the caller already has. `Some` continues an existing keyset/cursor
page; `None` with `include_total: false` (the default) still runs in
cursor mode, starting from the beginning of the set — see
`config.query.cursor_default`. `page`/`page_size` (offset math) are
ignored whenever cursor mode is in effect.

delta_token.description:
L7-T4: a delta token from an earlier answer, or `latest` for a first
one: answer the changes since it among the rows this query selects
(`EntityDelta`: created, updated, deleted, next_token) instead of a
page. A query over one entity only. `410 resync_needed` once the token
is older than the change feed keeps.

entity.description: Fallback: entity name string — backend derives UUID via entity_info

entity_logical_name.description: Entity UUID (from entity_info) — backend looks up default view

include_total.description:
P-stored-query-containment phase 2 / D-126: `true` is the only way to
get an exact `COUNT(*) OVER()` total — the full-set window scan is
expensive enough (audit finding #25) that it is opt-in, not the
default, now that cursor mode (below) is the default execution mode.
Defaulting this to `false` (was `true` pre-phase-2) is the one
behavioral flip this plan makes to the wire contract.

order_dir.description:
`"asc"` or `"desc"` — see `Filter::op`'s doc comment for why this
isn't expressed as a JSON-schema `enum` constraint (P-api-contract
Phase 0 disclosure: same reason applies here).

page.description:
One-based — the first page is `page=1` (D-347). Unlike the platform's
`GET` list endpoints, which clamp an out-of-range page, this one rejects
`page < 1` with 422; `page > 10000` is likewise rejected rather than
clamped, to push large scans onto `after_id` (D-031).

query_version_id.description:
D-521 — pinned execution: run this exact immutable
`sql_query_version` instead of the query's current SQL. The
version must belong to the resolved query and the query must still be
active. Only the SQL text, relation inventory and cost estimate come
from the pinned version; `required_privilege`, record-level scope and
the cost ceiling are evaluated at run time exactly as for an unpinned
call (pinned SQL, live security). A published dashboard records the
version each widget was published with and executes it through this.

oneOf.description:
M01 Core P3 gap (D-455) — narrows a single-entity query to rows
linked, through a named M:M relationship, to one anchor record on
the relationship's other side. `AppError::Validation` (422) for a
multi-entity/custom-SQL query (`entity_logical_name.is_some()` is
false — there is no single attribute set / entity for a relationship
to resolve against, the same D-057 boundary record-level RLS
scoping already draws in this file) or for a relationship that
exists but does not connect this query's entity.

seek.description:
AA4-T4: start a keyset page at this sort value ("jump to M", "jump
to March"): the first page holds the rows whose `order_by` value is
at or after it (at or before it for `desc`), with a `next_cursor` as
usual. Coerced and bound like a filter value on the sort column, so a
value of the wrong type is a 422; no rows are counted to find the
place. Not with `after_id` (422).

select.description:
S1-T1: the attributes to return, in this order; `id` is always
included. Absent returns the query's full column list. A name the
query does not return, or one the caller may not read, is the same
422 `unknown attribute`.

view_id.description: Direct list/view selection. The view resolves to its referenced SQL query.

ExitOn.description: Why a contact leaves a sequence.

ExpiredFlag.description: T6-T1: a flag past its expiry date, for the expiry report.

ExplainResponse.description: What the planner expects of a query; nothing is run.

guard_limit.description: The cost above which the query would be refused.

plan_class.description: `scan` when the plan reads the whole root table, else `index`.

ExplainStep.description: One step of why a person is in a list or not.

holds.description: Whether the step's list holds the person.

member_after.description: Whether the person is in after this step.

step.description: `base` (the list's own query or members), then each combination.

value_display.description:
A readable value where one is safe to show: a built-in `@current_user`
shows only the caller's own user name.

ExplainedPassage.description: One retrieved passage and the terms that brought it.

matched_terms.description: Terms found in the title, headings or passage.

matching_rows.description:
How many rows matched the filter when the export was accepted (the
worker re-resolves the caller's scope when it runs, so the file can be
smaller if access was revoked in between).

ExportPartLink.description: A23-T10: one file of a completed export, to download.

columns.description:
Requested column projection. Empty means "every column the caller
can currently read" — resolved fresh by the worker, not frozen at
request time.

labels.description:
A23-T10: CSV and XLSX headers in the requester's language (`id` and
`row_version` keep their names).

split_rows.description:
A23-T10: rows per file part of a Parquet export, 1 000 000 by default;
the status lists every part.

parts.description: A23-T10: every file of the export (one unless it was split).

stream_token.description:
L7-T5: a change-stream cursor that continues from the export's own
snapshot: reading a subscription from it yields exactly the changes
the export did not see.

result_type.description: The language type of the result (`number`, `text`, `bool`, ...).

sql_reason.description: Why it does not, when it does not.

sql_translatable.description: Whether the expression runs in the database as a filter.

value.description: The value for the sample record, when one was given.

ExpressionDiagnostic.description:
One problem with the expression. `start`/`end` are byte offsets into the
expression; absent when the error has no single place (a length limit).

ExpressionTraceStep.description: One evaluated sub-expression, in evaluation order.

FacetCount.description: One facet value and how many results have it.

FavouriteItem.description: One kept item, as the caller may see it now.

deleted.description: A record deleted since it was kept.

FavouriteItemInput.description: One item to keep in a list.

entity.description: The record's entity; required for a record.

label.description: What to show; a record's own name wins when it has one.

ref.description: The record id, the view id, or the page's route.

FavouriteList.description: One list: the caller's own (`team_id` null) or a team's.

FavouriteListInput.description: A list's whole content, as saved.

items.description: In display order.

FeatureFlagPolicy.description:
The stored policy value for one flag (`setting.value` under the
`feature.*` namespace). All three targeting tiers the M95 plan calls for,
plus the optional progressive-rollout percentage, live in one blob — see
the module doc for why.

expires_on.description:
T6-T1: when the flag should be gone; listed by the expiry report from
the day after. It changes nothing by itself.

owner.description: T6-T1: who answers for the flag (a name, an email or a user id).

percentage.description:
`0..=100`. When present, `deployment: true` is additionally narrowed
to a deterministic hash-of-user-id bucket of that size — the same
user always lands on the same side of the line while the percentage
stays fixed, and a wider rollout only ever adds users, never drops
one already in.

role_overrides.description:
Privilege key -> override. A caller holding any matching privilege is
in scope; "most permissive role wins" if more than one matches (same
posture the record-level access-level resolution uses elsewhere in
this codebase). Checked after `user_overrides`, before the
deployment/percentage tier.

schedule.description:
T6-T1: changes to the deployment value and rollout that take effect at
a time. The latest one whose time has come replaces `deployment` and
`percentage`; overrides stay as stored.

team_overrides.description:
T6-T1: team id -> override, checked after the user's own and before
the privileges'. A person in several teams gets `true` if any says so.

unit_overrides.description:
T6-T1: organisation (unit) id -> override, matched against the units
the person reaches (`SecurityContext::accessible_org_ids`), after
teams. A person resolved without units is never matched.

user_overrides.description: Stringified user UUID -> explicit override. Highest precedence.

actor.description: Who posted, or who made the change, when known.

entity.description:
A record event's entity, record and operation (`create`, `update`,
`delete`, `restore`).

id.description: The post's id, or the change event's.

record_name.description: The record's primary name, when its entity declares one.

FeedItemKind.description: What a feed item is. Ordered by wire name, as the keyset compares it.

FeedbackStats.description: Votes on turn answers written in the window.

answers.description: Rateable messages: an assistant message with a terminal state.

rated_answers.description: Answers with at least one vote.

FeedbackView.description: The caller's current vote on one answer.

api_protocol.description:
The protocol the listing was performed under, echoed so a UI can label
results that arrived before an operator changed the field.

FieldChangeResult.description: What a structure change did, or (dry run / blocked) would do.

applied.description: The change committed (or, for a large table, was queued: see `run_id`).

archived.description: Values archived by this call (0 while a large run is still going).

error.description:
A stable refusal code when the change is blocked
(`rename_blocked_by_reference`, `field_referenced`, `field_in_use`,
`archive_key_missing`, ...); `blockers` lists why.

labels.description:
Labels applied by these changes: "runs without business rules or
workflows" on a conversion.

not_convertible.description: Values that do not convert (dry run: would become empty).

nulled.description: Values nulled by a conversion (0 while a large run is still going).

records_with_value.description: Records that keep a removed choice value (shown empty).

report.description:
Release-report items (also stored in the report): breaking API changes,
adjusted/removed customer objects, archived/nulled values.

run_id.description:
The batched run of a large table (`GET .../data-steps/{run_id}` lane
P2-C/E; the run row is `data_step_run`).

sample_record_ids.description: Up to ten record ids of non-convertible values (ids only).

values_to_archive.description: Non-null values the delete archives (dry run: would archive).

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

key_a.description:
Each record's key for a key comparator (phone, email, id, name,
phonetic); `null` otherwise or when the record has none.

score.description: 1 matched, 0 differed, `null` no evidence (a side without a value).

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

mask_format.description:
Q15-T1: `last4`, `email`, `phone` or `full` when the profile shows the
field only masked; absent when it shows it in full.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this member row.
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this profile.

allow_sensitive.description: Required to list an `is_sensitive` field at all.

oneOf.description:
The viewer is authorized to see this value, but this API does not
decrypt it yet — see this module's doc comment.

Hidden: the viewer cannot currently read this field (I7), the whole
record's access has been revoked, or the value is `Restricted`-mode
and `audit.view_sensitive` does not exist yet (Phase 6.6).
Erased via a DSR/retention erasure pass.

FileCheckoutStatus.description: `GET …/checkout`: the lock, when one is held.

import_job_id.description: The import job whose staged rows to profile.

uploaded_by.description: The staff uploader; `None` for a portal user's upload (D-774).

uploaded_by_portal_user.description: The portal uploader, for a portal user's upload (D-774).

Filter.description:
P-api-contract Phase 0 disclosure: the retired hand-written
`openapi/query-v1.json` declared `op` as a JSON-schema `enum` of the 8
operator strings in this doc comment. Reproducing an exact `enum`
constraint on a plain `String` field (as opposed to a real Rust enum)
needs utoipa's `schema_with` escape hatch, whose exact builder-call shape
this session could not verify against the installed utoipa version — no
Rust toolchain in this sandbox (see the `no-rust-toolchain` memory /
DECISIONS.md entry for this change). Left as a documented, lower-fidelity
field (doc comment + example) rather than guessing at unverified macro
internals; re-add the `enum` constraint via `schema_with` once a human
can compile-check it — tracked as a Phase 0 follow-up, not silently
dropped. Runtime validation is unaffected either way: every caller's own
`match f.op.as_str()` is untouched by this OpenAPI-only annotation.

op.description:
One of: `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `contains_any`,
`contains_all`, `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`,
`is_null`, `is_not_null`. `starts_with`/`ends_with` are text-only,
like `contains`; `neq` excludes a stored NULL (SQL `<>`), exactly like
every other comparison — `is_null` is the only way to match one. The
four were added by D-607 (advanced find, B-R10 Phase A): the entity
grid had offered them since C-28 while the server refused them. For a
multi-select Choice:
`contains` tests one option, `contains_any` matches any supplied
option, and `contains_all` matches every supplied option. `in` matches
any of a non-empty string array by typed equality (not valid for a
multi-select Choice). `is_null` takes no value and matches a stored
NULL — the only way to express a NULL bucket (dashboard 10/10 Phase 0
spike S1). `under` and `above` (A17-T2) take a record id for a lookup
into a tree (an entity with one parent lookup to itself) and match
that record and everything below it, or above it, up to 32 levels.
`tagged` (B4-T4) takes a tag id on the `id` field and matches the
records carrying that tag (a personal tag only for its owner).

value.description:
Scalar filters retain the v1 string contract. Multi-select Choice
filters additionally accept a JSON string array for `contains_any`
and `contains_all`; `in` takes a string array; `is_null` ignores it.

FilterOrigin.description:
Where an applied filter came from — carried to the response so the
explanation (Phase 3.2) and the records drill use the same list.

attribute.description: The attribute, when the finding is about one.

created_at.description:
A folder is a virtual grouping, not a single row, so this is the
earliest timestamp among everything that makes the folder exist: the
explicit `document_folder.created_at` if it was created
empty, and/or the earliest `created_at` of any document living under
it. `NULL` only when the folder path predates the standard
`created_at` column on some pre-provisioned tables.

folder.description:
Full path from the record's root, e.g. `uploads/Contracts` — pass
straight back as the next request's `folder` param to drill in.

entity.description: The entity's logical name, as the record API addresses it.

ai.description: An AI attribute (N11-T1): `record.ai_field` can suggest its value.

attribute.description: The attribute's logical name: the key of its value in a record.

captcha_token.description: The solved challenge, when the deployment asks for one.

fields.description:
The form's fields, consent checkboxes (`consent_<purpose>`), UTM tags
and `page_url`, as the form sent them.

failing_checks.description: The checks the last run failed (or skipped).

period_days.description: How old a passing run may be.

FromListBody.description: Adding a list to a campaign.

list_id.description: The marketing list whose people become members.

purpose.description:
The consent purpose; required for an email, social, advertising or
content campaign.

consent_checked.description: Whether people without consent for the purpose are skipped.

admin_override.description:
P-data-protection-governance §4 cross-border transfer gate. Set only
once an admin has separately confirmed the export destination is
authorized to receive out-of-region restricted data — every use is
logged (`tracing::warn!`), never silent.

id.description: The DSR request this export fulfilled.

since.description: The language version that added it.

GanttBaselineItem.description: One item's planned dates in the baseline.

GapTopic.description:
A row of the authors' knowledge-gap queue (D-452; surfaced by D-489).

The phrase is the scrubbed topic, never the caller's raw question — read
[`normalize_gap_phrase`]'s doc before widening anything here, and D-452
before changing what a row stores.

addressed_item_ref.description:
The Knowledge Base item that addressed this gap (D-489, migration
0300). No FK: the target is a runtime-provisioned entity table.

addressed_page_ref.description: The content page that addressed this gap, from the 0263 shape.

sequence.description: Position in the technician's route, 1 first.

travel_minutes.description: Travel to this visit, in minutes (0 when not known).

row_version.description: The definition's current `row_version`.

GoogleConfigInfo.description:
P-frontend-baseline step 5 (D-071/D-073) — closes the config-debt item:
the Google OAuth client id (`config.auth.oauth_google_client_id`, already
the value `google_login` verifies the ID token's audience against) is
served from here instead of being duplicated as a hardcoded literal in
Angular's `environment.ts`. Same "public directory, never a secret" shape
as `OidcProviderInfo` — a client id is not sensitive (it's visible in any
browser's network tab once the Sign-In button loads), only
`oauth_google_client_secret` must never leave this struct.

client_id.description:
`None` when Google sign-in isn't configured for this deployment — the
login page renders no Google button, same as an empty OIDC directory.

GovernanceView.description:
The governance in effect for a conversation's session — snapshotted when
it started (D-505), shown whatever state the session is now in.

state.description:
`"live"` | `"paused"` | `"ended"` — ended covers revoked, ended and
expired alike.

tainted.description: Whether the session started downstream of tool-obtained content (I-10).

governed_change.description:
Changes to the domain's entities wait for its owners' or stewards'
approval at publish.

GrantView.description:
A grant as stored, with the G-3 label: `public` when no condition is bound
to the portal user, which only a read-only grant may be.

hidden.description: Nodes the caller may not see, counted only.

edge_type.description:
`"lookup:{field}"`, `"hierarchy:{field}"`, or `"relationship:{type}"`
— typed by source, per the plan's response contract.

Grounding.description:
Whether a turn's answer is grounded in retrieved knowledge. Decided from
the turn's executed knowledge actions alone — never from the answer text.

Group.description: One group of an aggregate result.

keys.description: Each group field's value (a bucket's start for a date bucket).

cause_group.description: The group to replay, from the groups list.

rate_per_minute.description: Items per minute after the preview; default 60, at most 600.

job_id.description:
The batch job replaying the rest (`GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}`); `None`
when the preview was the group's only item.

preview.description: The first item, replayed at once.

oneOf.description: Present only for a time bucket; the field must then be a date field.

expires_in_days.description:
