MyWorkAction.description:
One authoritative action a caller may take on a [`MyWorkItem`] — never
business logic of its own, only a pointer to the route that already owns
it. Dashboard (or any other caller) invokes `route` directly; the
provider never evaluates the action, only names it (the plan's "Dashboard
implements no business rule").

key.description:
Stable key for the action, e.g. `"approve"`, `"reject"` — not
displayed directly.

method.description: HTTP method the action's route expects.

route.description:
The authoritative route, with the item's own ids already substituted
(e.g. `/api/v1/approvals/{id}/decide`) — never a template the caller
has to fill in.

MyWorkItem.description: One actionable work item, from whichever provider owns it.

actions.description:
Resolved once, at list time, under this same visibility rule —
`actions()` re-resolves them fresh at click time, since eligibility
can change between the two (the plan's "checked at list time and
again at action time").

priority.description:
Free-form, provider-defined (`"high"`/`"1"`/...) — Dashboard does not
interpret it beyond display.

provider.description:
The provider's own `name()` — lets a caller group/filter without a
second lookup. Owned, not `&'static str`: `#[derive(Deserialize)]`
cannot prove a borrowed field outlives an arbitrary deserializer
lifetime, and every construction site already has a `&'static str`
literal to hand, so `.to_string()` there costs nothing that matters.

row_version.description:
The optimistic-concurrency version the item's `actions` routes expect
back, when they take one — for an approval that is the approval
request's current `row_version`, which `POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/
decide` requires. Omitted (`None`) by every provider whose actions
need no version.

source_entity.description:

the record or run its own further checks.

state.description: The record's own state/status label, for display only.

([`CursorPage`]): `next_cursor` is omitted on the last page.

members.description: The other people: exactly one for `direct`.

`settings`/`is_template`/`template_category`/`template_version`): those
are either operator-scoped concerns an authoring caller has no basis to
set, or edited afterward through ordinary generic entity CRUD once the
dashboard exists.

items.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/resources/capacity` — a single resource's
capacity/demand picture over the requested `[from, to]` period (M72).
See `capacity.rs`'s module doc for the exact arithmetic behind each
field — in short: `capacity_hours` is the platform's default business
calendar over the period, net of approved leave; `allocated_hours` is
`resource_allocation.allocation_percent` prorated by date overlap;
`actual_hours` is `project_time_entry.hours`, unrelated to either.

actual_hours.description:
`SUM(hours)` from `project_time_entry` for this resource, entries
dated within `[from, to]` — what was actually logged, independent of
what was planned.

allocated_hours.description:
`SUM(allocation_percent / 100 * capacity_hours * overlap_days /
period_days)` across every `resource_allocation` row overlapping
the period — prorated against the period's nominal (pre-leave)
capacity, not the leave-adjusted figure above; see `capacity.rs`.

capacity_hours.description:
Business-calendar working hours over `[from, to]`, net of any
`resource_availability` leave overlapping the period.

over_allocated.description:
`allocated_hours > capacity_hours` — the resource is committed past
what the period's business calendar (net of leave) can deliver.

resource_name.description:
`user_account.user_name` — `None` for a legacy row with no
username set, same optionality the column itself carries.

utilization_pct.description:
`allocated_hours / capacity_hours * 100`; `0.0` when `capacity_hours`
is `0` (e.g. a period with no working days at all, or a resource on
leave for the whole period) rather than a division-by-zero `NaN`.

items.description: One record of any entity. P-api-contract Phase 1: the platform dispatches generic CRUD from runtime metadata (D-003), so `data`'s property names differ per entity and per deployment and cannot be enumerated in a static document — call `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields. Everything outside `data` is the same on every entity.

approval_request_id.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): present only on the response to an update that
asked for a state transition requiring approval. The record was moved
to the transition's pending state (visible in `data`) instead of the
requested one, and this is the approval request that decides it
(`/api/v1/approvals/{id}/decide`). Omitted on every other response, so
those stay byte-identical.

created_at.description:
UTC ISO-8601. Typed `Value` in Rust because it is read straight out of
the dynamic row, but it is always a timestamp string or `null`.

data.description:
The record's own columns, keyed by attribute logical name. Values are
whatever the attribute's field type maps to in JSON.

duplicate_warnings.description:
A15-T4: the existing records this create or update matches under a
`warn` (or reasoned `allow_with_reason`) duplicate rule — the write
succeeded. Omitted when there are none.

expanded.description:
S1-T4: with `?expand=`, the records the named lookups point at, keyed
by lookup attribute; a target the caller may not read is absent.

held_attributes.description:
M9-T2: the attributes this update asked to change that an approval
process watches. They keep their stored values (visible in `data`)
until `approval_request_id` is approved. Omitted when nothing was
held.

hidden_duplicates.description: A15-T4: how many more matches the caller may not read. Omitted when 0.

labels.description:
S1-T13: present when the request named a language (`Accept-Language`
`ar` or `en`): each choice field's value as its label in that
language (a list for a multi-valued field), the value itself where no
label is written. `data` keeps the stored values.

lookups.description:
P-entity-contract-hardening item (a) â€” supersedes D-057's read-time
nulling (DECISIONS.md). `data` always carries the stored UUID for a
lookup field, unmodified; this sibling map carries the tombstone
metadata a client needs instead of a fabricated `null`. `None` (and
therefore omitted from the JSON body â€” `skip_serializing_if`) for any
entity with no populated lookup fields, so a non-lookup entity's
response is byte-identical to before this field existed.

merged_hidden.description:
A16-T2: how many more such attributes the caller may not read.
Omitted when 0.

merged_into.description:
A15-T5: this record was merged into that one (the entity keeps merged
records); omitted otherwise.

merged_over.description:
A16-T2: on an update sent with `If-Match-Merge: attributes` over a
stale version, the attributes others changed since that version,
which the update was merged over. Omitted otherwise.

warnings.description:
D-791 rule 6: the `warning`-severity business-rule `error` policies
that fired on this create, update or upsert — the write succeeded;
the form shows them. Omitted when there are none (and on reads), so
every other response stays byte-identical.

Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

items.description:
One passage returned from the knowledge corpus, with everything a citation
needs to resolve (`P-knowledge-base` §8, §11).

Every field is captured at projection time or computed here, never
reconstructed from the article at render time: an item edited after the
answer was generated would otherwise produce a citation pointing at a
heading that no longer exists.

kind.description:
D-429 (+ chart, migration 0447) — how this view renders: `list`
(default), `kanban`, `calendar`, `timeline`, `chart`. Kind-specific
settings live in `view_metadata`.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this view: `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer
may update or retire a system view (409 `layer_mismatch` otherwise).
Personal and shared views are user data and always `project`.

scope.description:
D-429 — always `system` through this admin surface; `personal`/
`shared` views are created and promoted only through the self-service
`/api/v1/views` routes below.

view_metadata.description:
D-429 — kind-specific settings, advisory only. Never a source of
server-side enforcement: a kanban `state_field`/`wip_limits` never
substitutes for `attome-state`'s own transition checks, a
calendar/timeline `start_field`/`end_field` never substitutes for the
view's own privilege/record-security gate, and a chart's
`x_field`/`y_fields`/aggregation never substitutes for `query/execute`
actually returning that column (see `chart_view_metadata`'s doc
comment).

omitted when empty.

items.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/project/{id}/work-items/rollup` — a work item's
own stored fields plus its point rollup. The client builds the WBS tree
from `parent_work_item_id`, the same flat-list-plus-parent-pointer shape
`entity/document-folder/document-folder-browser.component.ts` already
renders recursively.

is_critical_path.description:
Critical Path Method result — see `critical_path.rs` for the
algorithm and its documented scope (`finish_to_start` dependencies
only). `false`/`None` (not an error) when the project's dependency
graph has a cycle, or when this item isn't part of the dependency
network at all (an isolated item's float is trivially `0`, so it IS
still marked critical — only a genuine cycle degrades to `None`).

points_completed.description:
Sum of `points` over every leaf *descendant* of this node (itself,
if this node is a leaf).

points_own.description:
This node's own `points` value — meaningful only when it is itself a
leaf (`points_total == points_own` in that case); 0 for a
phase/parent row regardless of what its `points` column happens to
hold, per the "parent tasks and phases do not carry their own
progress" rule.

progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100`; `0.0` when `points_total`
is `0` (no leaf descendants yet, e.g. an empty phase).

D-521 — one widget's pinned query version in the live snapshot. A pinned
dashboard keeps running `pinned_version_id` until it is republished;
`newer_version_available` tells an editor that a republish would pick up a
changed query. `query_active` false means the pinned SQL will not run at

mode.description:
`phone` (the default: ring your own phone, then the number) or
`browser` (J6-T2: the softphone dials, through the TwiML app, with
the returned `call_id` as its `CallRef`).

system_id.description: Which voice system; the first active one when left out.

record_id.description:
`None` = a whole-entity hold. Not validated as "must currently
exist" — a hold may legitimately be placed ahead of a record's
creation (e.g. a litigation matter naming a customer before their
first record in a new entity exists) or survive the record's own
soft-delete; `record_is_held`'s check is by id match, not by live
row existence.

PlaceLegalHoldResult.description:
M15 (Data Governance, D-413) steward-defaulting hook: `place_hold`'s
response — every `LegalHoldSummary` field plus one additive
`resolved_steward_ref`, rather than nesting `LegalHoldSummary` inside a
wrapper object, so this stays a backward-compatible superset of the
pre-D-413 response shape (guidelines §12: prefer additive changes) — a
caller reading only the original fields sees no change.
`resolved_steward_ref` is the accountable steward for the held entity's
data domain, resolved at placement time via
`attome_core::resolve_steward_for_domain`. Purely informational — it
does not gate or route the hold, it just tells the placing admin who else
should probably know about it (matches the M15 plan §3 "steward is the
default reviewer" intent, for the one queue in this crate that actually
has entity context at creation time; see `governance_admin.rs`'s header
for why `dsr_admin.rs`'s DSR queue does not get the same hook in this
pass). `None` when the entity has no assigned domain, or its domain names
neither a steward nor a deputy.

guide_id.description: An order guide whose offerings join the order with `guide_answers`.

title.description: The order's title; "Order of N items" when unset.

reason.description: Why, for `Blocked`; a short note for `Retire`; `None` otherwise.

One ledger row without its `bundle`/`plan` payloads — the list shape the
M92 Phase 1 lifecycle UI reads. `bundle_name`/`bundle_version` are pulled
out of the row's already-fetched `bundle` JSONB (no extra query) so the
UI can group applied plans into "installed bundles" and offer rollback
targets without a second endpoint — `None` for an anonymous
whole-deployment plan (`Bundle.name` unset).

PlanResponse.description: `mode=plan` response — the persisted plan, as the approver sees it.

applicable.description: `blocked` is empty — apply would run this plan to completion.

basis_hash.description:
Hash of the live export the plan was computed against; `mode=apply`
refuses (409) once live metadata no longer hashes to it.

PlanRow.description:
One ledger row as the routes and the apply job see it. `bundle` and
`plan` are the JSON snapshots frozen at plan time (see the migration's
header for why they are stored rather than re-fetched).

cursor.description: Index of the next plan entry to apply; a resumed run starts here.

PlanStatus.description: Lifecycle of one plan row. The string form is the `status` column value.

PlannedOp.description: One operation's line in a plan.

risky.description: Phase 1 criteria: a contract operation, or a field made required.

applicable.description: Nothing in this phase is blocked.

apply_id.description:
The ledger row; `None` for a changeset that is already applied or
blocked before any row was written.

PolicyDef.description:
One policy, in the wire shape `{ type, field?, message?, severity?,
value?, expression?, mode? }` (one `rule_policy` row). Its shape
is checked by [`validate_rule`] (and by the table's CHECK); use
[`PolicyDef::effect`] for the typed view.

enforce_from.description:
A3-T4: with `stage: enforce`, the first day the check refuses writes;
before it the check warns.

expression.description: A `set_value` `attome-rules` expression over the entity's own fields.

oneOf.description: A3-T4: how this check is rolled out; absent means its severity decides.

status.description:
`requested` while its approval waits, then `approved`, `rejected` or
`expired`.

One entity the caller's role has a grant on. Its actions and fields:
`GET /{keyword}/api/v1/metadata/{entity}`.

PortalEntityView.description: One entity as a portal may see it in metadata.

PortalFieldView.description: One field as a portal may see it in metadata (web-portal plan Phase 5).

label.description: The field's display label, when it has one.

lookup_entity.description:
For a lookup the caller may pick a value for: the target entity. Set
only when the caller's role reads that entity, so a form can offer its
records; `None` for every other field, including the portal user field
the engine stamps.

options.description:
A choice field's options; `None` for every other type (a formula's
expression or a masked text's settings never reach a portal).

email.description: D-777: optional when the account has a username.

profile.description:
The fields this portal lets its users edit, with their values (empty
when none are editable).

row_version.description: The profile's version: send it as `If-Match` on `PATCH /me`.

username.description: D-777: the login username, when the account has one.

PortalRecord.description:
A record as a portal sees it: only allowlisted fields, no owner,
organisation or staff attribution columns.

PortalRoleKey.description:
A web-portal role's natural key: the portal's `keyword` and the role's
`name` (unique per portal, `webportal_role_name_unique`).

mfa_enrollment_required.description:
The portal requires MFA and this user has no usable authenticator
(never enrolled, or signed in with a recovery code since): only the
MFA enrollment and logout routes are available until they enrol.

recovery_code_used.description: This sign-in spent a recovery code (D-588 item 1).

current.description: The session this request was made with.

PortalSettingsPatch.description:
Every field optional except `row_version`. `owning_team_ref` distinguishes
"absent" (unchanged) from `null` (cleared).

resolved_entity_name.description:
Set once the work request is converted (`convert.rs`) — `ticket |
project_work_item | project`, mirroring `resolved_entity_name`.
Deliberately NOT `resolved_record_id`: an anonymous caller holding
only a status token has no privilege on whatever that id names, and
handing it out would invite probing the destination record directly.

email.description: D-777: optional when the user has a username.

username.description:
D-777: the login username (case kept); optional when the user has an
email.

further: every program under the portfolio, and every project under each
of those programs.

created.description: False when the source was posted before and this is that entry.

PowChallenge.description:
A proof-of-work challenge: find an `answer` such that SHA-256 of `nonce`
followed by `answer` starts with `difficulty` zero bits, then send
`{challenge}:{answer}` as the request's `captcha_token`.

PrecheckBody.description: A message to check before sending.

recipients.description:
The audience: how many, how many never mailed before, how many with
an invalid address.

text.description: The plain-text part, if the message has one.

detail.description: What matched (a phrase, a domain), when there is one.

guidance_key.description: The screens' translation key for what to do about it.

PrecheckSeverity.description: How much a finding costs the score.

resolved.description:
`true` once the outcome-fill sweep has recorded whether this
prediction actually came true (see `crate::score::fill_outcomes`).

PreferencesBody.description: The caller's preferences, replacing what was there.

Presentation.description: Modifiers applied on the server over the computed buckets.

other_bucket.description:
Fold the groups past `limit` into one explicit Other bucket. Needs
`limit` and a plain field group.

oneOf.description:
Defaults to `value_desc` for a field group and `key_asc` for a time
bucket. Ties always break on the typed key, then the series key.

design.description: The email design (blocks, direction, width, colour).

minutes.description: How long the link works, 1 to 10,080 minutes; 60 when unset.

PreviewRecord.description: B5-T2: one record as the edit would change it.

after.description: The same attributes after the edit.

language.description: The render's locale, e.g. `ar-SA`; the deployment's when unset.

PreviewRow.description: One staged row as the preview shows it.

mapped.description: The mapped values; a sensitive attribute's value is `"•••"`.

PreviewWarning.description: One field the template names that rendered empty for this caller.

reason.description: `unreadable`: the caller may not read it on this record.

PrivilegeDef.description:
`privilege` — privileges are platform-minted per entity
(`{entity}.read` etc. through `ensure_privilege`) and are therefore never
retired by a bundle; they are carried so a custom privilege key a role
grant or sidebar item names exists on the target before the grant does.

ProFormaConverted.description: The new draft a pro forma invoice became.

Problem.description:
Why one item of a batch did not apply: a stable machine-readable `code`
(the same codes as `ErrorResponse.code` where one fits, e.g.
`version_conflict`), English `message`, and an optional `detail` object.

days.description: The days with counts, oldest first.

share.description: `done_by_agent / (done_by_agent + done_by_person)`; none while nothing was done.

ProcurementStep.description: What a submit, order, cancel or change did.

approval_id.description: The approval opened, when one was.

budget_warning.description: Set when the budget is over and the line only warns.

committed.description: The amount committed on the budget line after the step.

order_id.description: The purchase order made by an order step.

full_scan.description:
L6-T2: read every row; by default a table of more than 100,000 rows
is sampled.

ProgramSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/program/{id}/summary` — same D-368 read-time-rollup rule as
`ProjectSummaryResponse`, one level up: every number here is computed
fresh from the program's own child projects, never a stored aggregate.

actual_cost_total.description:
Same `is_sensitive`-derived security gate as
`ProjectSummaryResponse::actual_cost` — `None` unless the caller
holds read access to `project_resource_rate`.

weighted_progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100` across every leaf work item
of every project under this program; `0.0` when there are none yet.

ProjectArea.description: One sidebar area of a project, e.g. Game Ops → Bans.

ProjectSection.description:
An installed vertical: a top-level sidebar group that a vertical bundle
created. Bundles write their sidebar roots with `is_customized = true` and
no `module_key` (every `verticals/*/bundle.json` does), which separates
them from the platform's own seeded groups. Switching a project or an area
off only hides it (`sidebar.is_active = false`, through
`PATCH /api/v1/sidebar/admin/{id}`); its data and API stay reachable.

ProjectSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/project/{id}/summary` — the "Project Control Center" tiles.
Every count/percentage here is computed at read time from the current
state of the project's own fields plus its child work items/issues/change
requests — nothing is a stored/cached rollup (see `work_plan.rs`'s doc
comment for why).

actual_cost.description:
`SUM(time_entry.hours * resource_rate.internal_cost_rate)` across
this project's leaf work items, using each user's most recent rate as
of the entry (falls back to `None`-contributes-nothing when no rate
row exists for that user). Distinct from `budget_consumed` above,
which stays a PM-maintained input — this is computed at read time
from `project_time_entry`/`project_resource_rate`, the same
D-368 rule every other number on this response follows.

`None` (not `0.0`) when the caller lacks read access to
`project_resource_rate` — `internal_cost_rate` is `is_sensitive`,
and this field is derived from it, so it is gated the same way: a
plain `ProjectRead` caller does not automatically see it.

baseline_id.description:
The most recently captured baseline this project's variance fields
are computed against — `None` when no baseline has ever been
captured (`POST /project/{id}/baseline`). See `variance.rs`'s module
doc for exactly what each field below does and does not measure.

budget_at_completion.description:
Budget at Completion — `budget_amount`, unchanged; repeated here so
every EVM figure below reads from one self-contained group.

budget_consumed.description:
PM-maintained for this phase — see the implementation plan's
"Deferred" section (time-entry-driven automation is a follow-up).

cost_performance_index.description:
Cost Performance Index — `EV / AC` (`AC` is `actual_cost` above,
already gated on `project_resource_rate` read access — this
inherits that gate: `None` whenever `actual_cost` is `None`, same as
every other cost-derived field on this response). `> 1` means
under budget for work performed so far, `< 1` means over.

earned_value.description:
Earned Value — `BAC × weighted_progress_pct / 100`, the standard
"budgeted cost of work performed" formula using this project's own
live progress fraction. `None` without a `None` BAC.

estimate_at_completion.description:
Estimate at Completion — `BAC / CPI`, the standard "current cost
performance continues for the rest of the project" projection.

forecast_buffer_days.description:
`target_end_date - forecast_date`, in days. Positive means the
forecast lands before the target (buffer); negative means it lands
after (overrun). `None` unless both dates are present.

forecast_date.description:
`MAX(due_date)` among leaf work items not yet `done` — `None` when
every leaf item is done or the project has no leaf items yet.

health.description:
PM-maintained (`attome_project.health`), not auto-scored — see the
implementation plan's "Deferred" section.

planned_value.description:
Planned Value — `BAC × (baseline points whose planned_due has
already passed) / (baseline points total)`. A simplified,
points-as-progress-measure PV: this crate has no per-task budget to
time-phase (`project_work_item` carries no cost field — see
`baseline.rs`'s own doc comment on why `planned_budget` is always
`NULL`), so points stand in for value the same way `weighted_progress_pct`
already does for EV below. `None` without a baseline or a `None` BAC.

points_blocked.description:
Points belonging to leaf items whose status is `blocked` — a delivery
exposure metric, deliberately not netted out of `points_total` or
counted toward `points_completed`.

schedule_performance_index.description:
Schedule Performance Index — `EV / PV`. `> 1` means ahead of the
baseline's planned pace, `< 1` means behind.

schedule_variance_days.description:
The baseline's own planned finish (`MAX(planned_due)` across its
captured items) minus the live `forecast_date` above, in days.
Positive means the live forecast is ahead of the baseline's plan;
negative means it has slipped behind it. `None` when either date is
missing (no baseline, no baseline item carries a `planned_due`, or
every leaf item is currently `done` so there is no live forecast).

scope_item_count_variance.description:
Active work items now minus active work items captured in the
baseline — positive means scope has grown since the baseline,
negative means it has shrunk (items deactivated/deleted).

variance_at_completion.description:
Variance at Completion — `BAC - EAC`. Positive means the project is
trending to finish under budget.

weighted_progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100`, over the project's leaf work
items only (a phase/parent item never carries its own points — see
`work_plan.rs`). `0.0` when there are no leaf items yet.

work_items_done.description:
Leaf work items only ("actionable" — a phase/parent container is
never itself actionable).

messages.description: The messages in order, as sent: `role` and `content`.

otp.description: The customer's delivery code, when codes are on.

photo.description: A photo, already uploaded through the files API (its file key).

signature.description: A signature image, already uploaded (its file key).

cod_payment_id.description: The cash payment recorded for cash on delivery.

ProofSide.description: Which side of the running hash a sibling sits on.

ProofStep.description: One step up the tree: the sibling's hash (hex) and its side.

entries.description: The time entries the proposal took.

unrated_users.description: People with billable time but no billable rate, left out.

deliverable_id.description: The accepted deliverable, for a milestone.

until.description:
The last day of time taken, for time and materials (today when
absent).

work_order_ids.description:
The work orders to plan; by default the day's scheduled work orders
with no technician.

suggestion_id.description:
The row in `ai_suggestion_outcome` this suggestion was logged as.
The caller reports the human's decision against it.

ProviderDay.description: One provider's totals on one day.

PublicBookingPage.description: A booking page as the public sees it.

location.description: Where an in-person meeting is, or the number a phone meeting uses.

meeting_type.description: D20-T3: `video`, `phone` or `in_person`; none when the page does not say.

video_provider.description: The video service of a video meeting.

PublicBranding.description:
What the browser applies: the CSS variables the theme sets, and whether
to hide the vendor's name.

app_name.description: The product name to show, when the theme sets one.

PublicPageView.description:
Read-only shape served by the public, anonymous `content_public.rs`
route — deliberately narrower than `PageDetail`: no `id`/`row_version`/
`status`/draft blocks, nothing an anonymous visitor has any business
seeing.

approval_pending.description:
`true` when `dashboard.publish` is in `approval.required_actions` and
this call only submitted a pending four-eyes request — the fields
below are `None` in that case, and the dashboard is still `approved`,
not `published`, until a second admin decides the request.

PublishResult.description:
A publish's outcome: published (with its version), or waiting for
approval in a space that requires it (K5-T1).

approval_request_id.description: The approval request a publish waits for.

PublishedDashboard.description: D-521 — what a viewer of `dashboard_id` sees.

snapshot.description:
The version snapshot (`snapshot_format` 2 carries pinned
`dependencies`); `null` for `none`.

bundle_version.description:
The profile's bundle version (B18-T4): a different one means fetch the
profile again.

done.description: `true` once every profile entity is up to date; pull again later.

PulledRecord.description: A record to keep or update on the device.

record.description: The record's values, without sensitive attributes.

bytes_used.description: Bytes the device's offline store uses.

queue_size.description: Changes still waiting on the device after this push.

base_row_version.description: The row version the change was made against (update, delete).

base_values.description: The changed fields' values before the change (update).

changed.description: The fields changed and their new values (create, update).

client_op_id.description: The device's own id for this operation; a retry repeats it.

id.description: The record. For a create, the UUIDv7 the device gave it.

PutEmailSignature.description:
A signature to store. An empty `body` clears it. `row_version` is the one
last read (0 when there was none).

overlay.description:
An OpenAPI Overlay 1.0 document whose actions set summary,
description or example on this deployment's paths.

row_version.description: The overlay's current `row_version`; 0 when none is set yet.

PutQuerySharesBody.description: The whole share list of a query; it replaces the stored one.

Required when `scope` is `organization` or `user`; must be omitted
(or null) when `scope` is `deployment` — the same shape
`setting`'s CHECK constraint enforces at the database.

dimension_weights.description: Dimension name to weight (0 or more); unset dimensions weigh 1.

issue_sla_days.description: Days an issue is due in (default 7).

ids.description: The records, at most 500; give `ids` or `filters`.

dimension_weights.description: Dimension name to weight in the overall score.

QueryDef.description:
`sql_query` — one stored query. The key is `(entity, name)`;
`entity` is `None` for a multi-entity query (`entity_logical_name IS
NULL`). `name` is the table's `record_no` column, which is what every
admin surface calls the query's name.

entity_mappings.description:
The *current* published version's entity/id-column mappings
(`sql_query_entity_mapping`, D-146).

table_definition.description:
`sql_query.table_definition` — the editor's column JSON, kept
as the string the table stores.

entity_mappings.description:
P-stored-query-containment Phase 3 (D-146): the current published
version's admin-declared entity/id-column mappings — what
`query_exec.rs` splices a per-record RLS predicate against for a
custom/multi-entity query. Empty for a single-entity query (which
doesn't need one — see `entity_logical_name`) or a multi-entity query
that hasn't declared any mapping yet (still gated by the prior
all-or-nothing Global-scope-required check).

is_report.description: P1.1e: raises the read-only transaction's statement_timeout to 5s.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this query.

parameters.description: S4-T9: its declared parameters, `[{name, type, required}]`.

query_spec.description: S4-T9: the saved QuerySpec, run by id through `query/run`.

required_privilege.description:
P1.1e: when set, `query/execute` requires this exact privilege key
instead of the coarse admin-only default.

row_version.description:
C-19: `sql_query.row_version` (migration 0443) — send back as
`If-Match` on the next `PATCH` to guard against a lost update. Additive:
a caller that ignores this keeps behaving exactly as it did before this
column existed (`update_query`'s `If-Match` stays optional).

QueryEntityMapping.description: One `sql_query_entity_mapping` row, entity carried by logicalname.

rows_are_the_result.description:
True when the rows shown are the result (a query over more than one
entity); false when its buckets drill to records (P7-T1).

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this query — `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer may
change or retire it.

QueryRef.description: The logical key of a stored query, as referenced from a [`ViewDef`].

QueryShare.description: One share of a stored query.

QueryShareAccess.description: What a share lets its holders do; `edit` includes `read`.

QueuedDeliveries.description: M13-T4: what a test send or a replay queued.

delivery_id.description: The test delivery's id (test send only).

requests_per_minute.description: Requests per minute, 1 to 100,000; `null` clears the quota.

name.description: The person deciding, as they sign.

QuoteLineView.description: One line as the customer sees it.

unset.description: The deal's quotes that stopped being primary.

row_version.description: The quote's row version after the call.

status.description: `sent`, or `pending_approval` when it waits for the approval process.

QuoteTotals.description: The quote's totals from its lines and its own discount percent. Pure.

QuoteView.description: A quote as the customer sees it.

truncated.description: More accounts exist than a preview looks at.

ReauthRequiredResponse.description: A sensitive operation needs a fresh step-up on the caller's own session. Never an expired session: the client prompts for a step-up and must not refresh or sign out.

acceptable_factors.description:
The factors a step-up for this operation accepts now: `totp`,
`recovery_code`, `password` and `federated`, or the single
`totp_enrollment_required` when the account has none.

operation.description:
The protected operation, from the route: `identity_link` or
`api_key_create`.

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043).

example.message: re-authentication is required for this operation

RebuildRange.description: The rebuild job's payload: the UTC days to recount, both included.

after.description: The previous page's `next_after`; omit for the first page.

RecentItem.description: One recent record, as the caller may see it now.

deleted.description: Deleted since it was opened: restore it rather than open it.

label.description: The record's primary name, when its entity declares one.

items.description: Up to 50 opens, newest last.

Recommendation.description:
One recommendation on an approval request: approve or reject and why,
from an eligible approver or an agent acting for one. It decides nothing.

agent_session.description: The agent session that wrote it, when an agent did.

RecordContext.description:
The record the user is looking at, sent by the panel as a navigation hint
(I-19). Never authorization: see the module doc.

certificate.description: What was disposed, under which category, by whom and when.

RecordDispositionBody.description: A record whose disposition is asked for.

RecordHistoryChange.description: One change to a record: who made it, when, and which fields moved.

agent_session_id.description: The agent session that made it, when an agent did.

fields.description: Readable fields only, by field name.

group_id.description:
B2-T1: the change set it belongs to: `batch:<id>` (an import or bulk
action), `agent:<session>`, `run:<correlation id>` (a flow run or other
correlated work), `request:<id>` (one save), else `change:<audit id>`.
Changes with the same value were made together.

RecordHistoryField.description: One field's old → new pair within a change.

field_type.description:
The attribute's current field type (`text`, `number`, `date`, `bool`,
`choice`, `lookup`, …) so a client can render the values.

masked.description: True for a sensitive field: it changed, and its values are withheld.

old_lookup_name.description: For a lookup: the referenced records' names at the time of the change.

RecordRun.description: One record's outcomes, step by step.

error.description: Why the record stopped early, when it did.

RecordSelection.description: Which records a bulk operation covers: exactly one of the two.

owner_email.description: Every live record owned by the user with this email.

RecordSet.description:
Phase 3 reference data: rows of one entity keyed by a declared business
key (P-environment-promotion §5 step 24). `key_fields` name the row's
attributes that together form its identity (e.g. `["name"]` for a
notification template's unique key) — resolved to a live record's id at
*plan* time ([`super::plan::plan_bundle`]) and applied through the
ordinary entity-mutation primitives ([`super::apply`]).

A lookup field's value is either a literal id or a key reference to its
target — `{"key": {"name": "API Key"}}` — resolved to the one active target
row that key matches (D-534, [`super::record_sets`]'s module doc). Reference
data another bundle seeds must be named by key: its id differs between a
deployment that created the row and one where it predates that bundle.

**Never exported automatically.** Unlike every other component,
[`super::export::export_bundle`] never populates `record_sets` — `SELECT`
against an arbitrary metadata-defined entity table with no declared key
convention would have to guess what "the key" is, and a wrong guess
silently reference-datas the wrong rows on the next apply. A record set is
authored by hand (or by `bundle-tool`, given the target entity and key
fields explicitly) and merged into a bundle deliberately — the F273
vertical-pack convention this phase generalizes.

capability.description: `view` or `action` (`deny` rows are listed too, read-only).

RecordTypeChange.description: What a type change does, or did.

from.description: The record's type now (`null`: the entity's default type).

invalid_attributes.description: Attributes holding a value that the new type's form does not show.

row_version.description: The record's row version after the change.

clear.description: Attributes to clear; each must be one the preview lists.

row_version.description: The record's row version; required to apply the change.

RecordTypeOption.description: A27-T4: one record type the caller may create.

form.description: The form a record of this type shows, when it names one.

is_default.description: The type a new record gets when the caller names none.

RecordTypeStage.description: The stage a record of the new type starts in.

state_field.description: The attribute that holds the record's state.

retention_days.description: How long a record of this category is kept, in days.

RecordsPosture.description:
A single deployment-wide snapshot, not a list — same "aggregate summary,
not `PaginatedResponse<T>`" shape `attome_api::api_usage_admin`'s summary
endpoint already uses (guidelines §12 reserves the paginated envelope for
genuinely list-shaped access patterns).

past_retention_awaiting_disposition.description:
`audit_retention_action` rows still `status = 'proposed'` — records past
retention with no disposition decided yet.

RecoveryCodes.description: Single-use MFA recovery codes, shown once (D-588 item 1).

evidence_kind.description: The drill kind whose evidence proves it.

measured_rpo_seconds.description: What the newest passing drill measured.

proven.description: A fresh drill of that kind measured within the target.

resolution.description: What was corrected, or why the request was rejected.

currencies.description: One set of measures per currency.

week_start.description: First day of the business week (`sun`, `mon`, `sat`).

countries.description: The countries the pack presets, by code.

country.description:
The deployment's country (`core.country`), or null before the first
run picked one.

pack_available.description: Whether the regions pack is next to the server (`app.packs_root`).

id.description:
The id this device was given before, to refresh it; absent (or no
longer the caller's live device) registers a new one.

invitation_token.description:
P-registration-gating Phase 2 (D-128) — required (and validated) only
when `auth.registration_mode == "invite"`; ignored in `"public"` mode,
unreachable in `"disabled"` mode (the handler rejects before parsing
gets this far in spirit, though the body is still parsed first).

RegistrationConfigInfo.description:
P-registration-gating (D-128) — public directory-style config, same
"harmless because it's not a secret" shape as `GoogleConfigInfo`/
`OidcProviderInfo`: the Angular login page fetches this to decide whether
to render the sign-up form/link at all, instead of showing it and letting

RehearsalStepDto.description: One timed step on the copy.

RehearseRequest.description:
The change to rehearse: the field and its target contract; absent
values keep the field's current ones.

RejectedEvent.description: An event left out, by its place in the batch.

page_ids.description:
Neighbor page ids, nearest first. Empty on a deployment where no
chunk has an embedding yet (D-452) — Stage 2's backfill is what
populates `knowledge_chunk.embedding`; this route does not
depend on anything else that is unbuilt.

RelatedPagesBody.description:
Full-set replace for a page's symmetric "related pages" — the admin API
writes both directions (A→B and B→A) in one transaction, so a read for
either page's related list is a single-direction query.

id.description:
The anchor record's id, on the relationship's side OTHER than this
query's own entity.

RelationshipDef.description:
M01 Core P3 gap (D-455) — `relationship_info`, keyed by `name`.
`join_table` is intentionally NOT part of this definition even though
the live row stores it: it is a derived, deterministic function of
`name` (`"mm_{name}"`, `reconcile_relationship`'s own convention),

place the same fact could drift.

cascade.description:
`"restrict" | "orphan" | "cascade-deactivate"` — see
`attome_core::RelationshipCascade`. C-21 (M01 §7): the underscore
spelling `"cascade_deactivate"` this field wrote before the fix is
still accepted on apply for one release
(`RelationshipCascade::from_db_str`), but a fresh export always
carries the hyphenated form.

M01 Core P3 gap (D-455) — one `relationship_info` row touching
this entity, oriented from the entity's own point of view. This is what
makes the entity form's generic relationship sub-grid data-driven
instead of the per-entity hardcoded `xrm-related-grid` blocks the legacy
hand-built `_mm_` tables still need.

cascade.description:
`"restrict" | "orphan" | "cascade-deactivate"` (C-21, M01 §7 —
`attome_core::RelationshipCascade::as_db_str` always writes this
hyphenated spelling).

label.description:
The label THIS entity's own form should show for the sub-grid of
linked `other_entity` records — `role_b` when this entity is
`entity_a` (role_b is "B's role, *from A's point of view*" —
`RelationshipDef::role_b`'s own doc comment), and vice versa.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this relationship —
`platform | product | project | customer`.

apply_ids.description: The ledger rows (`changeset_apply.id`) of this apply run.

backup_retain_until.description: Keep the pre-apply snapshot at least until then (design §7.2).

release.description: Platform version and the changesets of the release.

building.description: Reports still building (an apply running or stopped mid-run).

last_release_at.description: When the newest report became ready.

record_ids.description: The records to render, 1 to 500; a repeated id renders once.

attached.description: Completed renders attached to their record.

D-525 — how the viewer renders a widget type. Only types with a real
renderer carry anything but `unsupported`; the palette hides the rest and an
existing widget of such a type renders an explicit "unsupported widget type"
state (and is reported by health).

from.description: Every delivery matched at or after this time is sent again.

reason.description: Why the source refused, for `refused`.

differing.description: Runs with at least one difference.

attachments.description: J1-T2: the record's own files to send with the reply, by file key.

has_values.description: The item carries sealed values (a conflict).

kind.description:
`conflict | conversion_nulled | field_deleted | customer_object_adjusted |
customer_object_removed | breaking_api_change | choice_removed_in_use |
required_empty`.

status.description: `open | info | accepted | used_mine | restored | dismissed | superseded | expired`.

values.description:
A conflict's `{theirs, ours, key}` (the customer's value, kept; ours;
the record's business key).

values_hidden.description: The values exist but the caller may not read the field.

ReportItemView.description: One item, with a conflict's values when the caller may read them.

created.description: False when this was a repeat of a stored request.

RequestAudit.description: An audit event a request wrote.

RequestLine.description: One line of an invoice request.

Requires.description: What a bundle needs from the deployment it is applied to.

depends_on_bundles.description:
M92 Phase 1 — other named bundles ([`Bundle::name`]) this bundle
assumes are already installed, and the floor version of each. Checked
at plan time against the ledger's own applied-bundle history
([`super::plan::check_bundle_dependencies`]): unlike
`platform_version`/`schema_version`/`modules` above (which
`check_requires` verifies purely, from arguments the caller already
has), this needs the ledger, so it is verified separately in
[`super::plan::plan_bundle`].

modules.description:
License module keys (`attome_modules::MODULE_MAP` names) the bundle's
content references. The exporter writes the distinct
`sidebar.module_key` values plus `core`.

platform_version.description:
A minimum server version, `">=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH"` (a bare
`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` is read the same way). The exporter writes the
exporting binary's own version.

schema_version.description:
The highest applied migration ordinal the bundle was exported against
— the floor the target must have reached (`attome_db::schema_state`).

message.description: The last status update; a standard text when absent.

page_id.description:
Scopes which declared `dashboard_variable`/`dashboard_parameter`
rows apply — omit for dashboard-level only.

remaining.description: Unrestored rows left for another request (per-field only).

skipped_filled.description: The record's field has a value now; never overwritten.

skipped_not_convertible.description: The archived value does not fit the field's current type.

archived_after.description: Only values archived at or after this time.

id.description: The DSR request.

condition.description: Filters the covered records must match, as the list views use.

start_attribute.description:
The date the period starts from: `created_at`, `modified_at` or a
date attribute of the entity.

RetentionRuleBody.description: A rule as an administrator writes it.

row_version.description: On an update, the version read; a newer stored version answers 409.

ReviewByBody.description:
Full replace, `null` clears — same convention as `SchedulePageBody`
(D-452's `review_by`, a plain `Option<NaiveDate>` full-replace, has no
empty-string-vs-null ambiguity to resolve).

ReviewDecision.description:
Which staged actions a review decision covers: one agent session's, or
chosen ones (at most [`MAX_REVIEW_IDS`]).

undo_window_seconds.description:
Apply only: hold the applied actions this many seconds (30 to 86400)
before they run, cancellable; omit to run them now.

jti.description:
The `jti` of the session to kill — from an audit/access log, or the
incident-response tooling that flagged the session as compromised.

RewindBody.description: Y7-T4: where to rewind a consumer to; exactly one of the two.

to_seq.description: The first event at or after this sequence number.

to_time.description: The first event written at or after this time.

approval_pending.description:
D-195 / P-four-eyes-approval — `true` when `approval.required_actions`
(attome-config) names `ACTION_SECURITY_REWRAP`:
this call did NOT enqueue the rewrap, it only submitted an approval
request. A second `system.admin` (never the same user) must decide it
via `POST /api/v1/admin/approvals/{id}/decide` before it actually runs.

RiskTier.description:
How much damage an action can do, which decides what has to happen before
it runs. This is the single most important field on a descriptor.

The tiers are ordered, and the ordering is load-bearing: an agent session
carries a ceiling and the gate compares against it. Adding a tier means
deciding where it sits relative to `Consequential`, which is a decision
somebody has to make deliberately.

fields.description:
Meaningful in `listed` mode; kept as stored in `legacy` mode, so
switching back to `listed` restores the list.

RoleDef.description:
`role` — one role with its grants, entity access rows and
field-security profile links. `owner_ref`/`owner_type` are deliberately
absent: the owner is a user or team, i.e. environment identity.

RoleEntityAccess.description:
One `role_mm_entity_access` row (D-133 per-entity depth,
0130's owner-visible flags).

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this access row.

read_owner_visible.description:
D-371 (amends D-357 ruling 2): orthogonal "I own this record"
visibility per action, independent of the depth columns above.

RoleGrant.description:
One role ⟷ privilege grant and its bounded record conditions
(`role_privilege_condition`, D-369).

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this condition row.

condition_count.description:
D-369: live `role_privilege_condition` count for this grant —
eager, not lazy-fetched per row, so the Role form's Privilege Grants
matrix can show a "Conditional" badge without an extra request per
grant (an N+1 a lazy per-row fetch would otherwise cause).

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this grant row.

ip_allowlist.description:
M03/D-434: per-role CIDR allow-list (`role.ip_allowlist`,
migration 0225) — `attome_server::middleware::auth::check_role_ip_
allowlist` enforces it on every request from a holder of this role.
`None`/absent means unrestricted, matching the column's `NULL`
default.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this role — `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer may
change it.

position_hierarchy_enabled.description:
F138: whether this role extends its `role_mm_entity_access`
depths down the holder's position subtree (see the
`position-hierarchy` endpoint in `role_entity_access`). Defaults to
`false` at the DB layer (migration 0053) — orthogonal to the
access-level ladder, not a fifth rung on it.

row_version.description:
C-19: send back as `If-Match` on the next `PATCH` to guard against a
lost update. Additive — a caller that ignores this keeps behaving
exactly as it did before `update_role` started honoring the header.

sso_only.description:
Only single sign-on, never a password, for every holder of the role
who is not a break-glass account.

id.description: `user_account_mm_role.id` — the assignment row, not the user.

allow_retire.description:
Same meaning as `import?mode=plan`'s `allow_retire`: without it, any
object present live (added by a version newer than `to_version`) but
absent from the target snapshot is reported `Blocked` rather than
retired.

to_version.description:
The named bundle's [`super::model::Bundle::version`] to roll back to.
Must match a `succeeded` ledger row's stored `bundle.version` for this
`name` — i.e. a version that was itself successfully applied before.

RollbackPreview.description: AH2-T4: what rolling an agent back would do.

session_ids.description: The agent's sessions since the time.

RollbackSince.description: AH2-T4: when to roll an agent back from.

since.description: Undo what the agent did at or after this time (UTC, ISO-8601).

RolloutReleaseReport.description:
The release report's open work (the fleet's notification rule reads
`last_report_id` and `open_items`).

building.description: Reports still building (an apply running or stopped mid-run).

last_report_id.description: The newest ready release report (an apply run, not a single change).

configuration_version.description:
The sha256 of this deployment's canonical metadata export (as
`/version`).

ledger_head.description: One row per (layer, scope), newest `seq` first within it.

pending_approvals.description:
Pending `metadata.changeset_apply` approval requests (an apply waiting
for a human on this server).

schema_version.description:
The highest applied SQL migration (as `/version`); `null` when the
migration table cannot be read.

is_set.description: Q18-T6: a credential is stored; no part of it is returned.

updated_at.description: When the stored credential was set.

RouteLatency.description: One route's request latency, from the request-duration histogram.

RuleDef.description:
M45 Phase 2 (D-472) — `rule`, keyed by `"{entity}:{name}"`.
`version` is deliberately NOT part of this definition (same posture
`AppDef` takes for its two excluded local UUID refs above): a bundle
carries the CURRENT definition, not a publish history, and the target
deployment always reconciles to `version = 1` on first apply — see
`COMPONENT_RULE`'s own doc comment.

**Business rules (D-789, D-791; `BUSINESS-RULES-DESIGN.md` §7).** A
`kind = "business"` definition carries `applies_to`, `roles` (staff role
names), `portal_roles` (`{portal, role}` natural keys), `condition` and
`policies` instead of `expression`/`target_field`/`message`. Every added
field is optional and skipped when empty, so an expression-kind definition
(and the canonical hash of a bundle that holds only those) is unchanged.

oneOf.description: Business rules: `all` (default) or `roles`.

expression.description: Legacy kinds only; absent on a business rule.

policies.description: Business rules: the ordered policies (list order is the ordinal).

portal_roles.description:
Business rules: web-portal roles by `{portal keyword, role name}`,
sorted.

roles.description: Business rules: staff role names (never UUIDs), sorted.

RuleEditorWarning.description: An editor warning (design §6.4). Never blocks a write.

RuleExplanation.description: One rule's outcome on a stored record (A11-T5).

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleIssue.description:
One validation problem, addressed by a path into the rule body
(`condition.all[1].value`, `policies[0].field`).

RulePreview.description: What a draft rule would flag over a sample.

examples.description: Up to 20 of them, highest score first.

pairs.description: Pairs the rule would flag among them.

RulePreviewPair.description: One pair a draft rule would flag.

RuleRejections.description: Refusals of one rule on one attribute through one channel.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name; `None` once the rule is deleted.

RuleRoleRef.description: One role a business rule applies to.

live.description:
`false` for a soft-deleted staff role: inert, dropped on the rule's
next save (design §1.1, §8.4).

portal.description:
The portal's keyword (portal roles only; `None` when the portal is
gone or the portal module is not installed).

portal_role.description: `true` for a web-portal role, `false` for a staff role.

record.description: The example record, attribute to value.

set_values.description: The values the rule's `set_value` policies must produce.

record.description: The record to evaluate against — no save, no side effects.

applies.description:
Whether the rule applies to the tested audience (always `true` when
no audience was given).

condition.description:
`true`, `false`, `unknown` (null, non-boolean or a failed evaluation:
locks and errors apply, `set_value` fails the write) or `transient`.

error.description:
An evaluation failure (budget, divide by zero, a `set_value` that
could not be computed).

policies_fired.description: Ordinals of the policies that fire.

result.description: Legacy kinds: the expression's raw value.

set_values.description: Field → the value each firing `set_value` policy writes.

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

RuleWarning.description:
A `warning`-severity `error` policy that fired on a successful write
(D-791 rule 6). Returned in the write response's `warnings` list and
logged; it never blocks. Carries names and the rule's own message, never a
record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RunGroup.description: One invoice request a run would make.

queued.description: False when a run was already queued.

params.description:
Overrides the report's default `parameters` entirely when non-empty
(not a deep merge) — same `Filter` grammar as `query/execute`.

RunRequest.description:
A query, as `spec` (the QuerySpec JSON form) or as `q` (its text form),
exactly one. `params` and `explain` apply to either; a text query takes
them only from here.

explain.description: Plan the query and return the plan's summary instead of rows.

q.description:
The text form: `SELECT … FROM … [WHERE …] [GROUP BY …] [HAVING …]
[ORDER BY …] [LIMIT n]`.

query_id.description:
S4-T9: run the stored query with this id (its saved QuerySpec);
`params` are its parameter values and `spec` and `q` are absent.

spec.description:
The QuerySpec: `entity`, `select`, `where` (a condition tree of
`and`/`or`/`not`/`compare`/`param`/`exists`/`not_exists` nodes, tagged
by `kind`), `sort`, `page_size`, `cursor`, `group_by`, `aggregates`,
`having`.

RunResponse.description: Rows (a keyset page), aggregate groups, or a plan.

RunRow.description: One result row, its columns by name (a related field by its path).

RunStarted.description: What a started run returns at once (N7-T1).

status.description:
`running`: follow `GET /api/v1/ai/conversations/{id}/stream` for its
steps and its end state.

RunToolCall.description: One tool call inside a turn of a run (N29-T1).

invocation_outcome.description: The invocation ledger's outcome for it, when it reached the ledger.

RunTree.description: A session's whole run as one tree (N29-T1).

battlecard_ref.description: The knowledge article holding the battle card, when one is set.

records.description: For a `manual` list: the records to add.

sent.description: The contacts a survey went to.

script_answers.description: The script's answers, as JSON text.

reason.description: Why the member is passed over (shown on the list).

move_splits.description: Move the old owner's splits to the new owner (else they stay).

old_owner_role.description:
Keep the old owner on the team with this team role; absent removes
them and their share.

needs_new_manager.description: The contacts who reported to this one and need a new manager.

new_contact_id.description: The new contact at the next account.

new_account_id.description: The account the person joined, if known.

roles.description: The account team roles to copy, e.g. `["account_manager", "pre_sales"]`.

SalesCpqProblem.description: One failure, for a person or an agent to act on.

percent.description: Decimal text, 0 to 100; null removes it.

opportunity_ids.description: The caller's open deals that miss at least one default member.

SalesFeedbackSkip.description: A contact the request did not reach, and why.

reason.description: `not_readable`, `no_consent`, `no_address` or `already_sent`.

snapshot_id.description:
D6-T8: for a deal discount, the snapshot that undoes it
(`POST /api/v1/sales/undo/{snapshot_id}`, 30 minutes).

previous_manager_id.description: The manager before this change: set it back to undo.

opportunity_competitor_id.description: The deal's competitor link, on a confirm.

previous_manager_id.description: The contact's manager before an accepted draft set it (to undo).

SalesOrgChartDraftDecision.description: Accept or reject an org chart draft.

accept.description:
`true` sets the proposed manager (and department); `false` only
marks the draft rejected.

render_id.description: The docgen render; read it at `GET /api/v1/docgen/renders/{render_id}`.

SalesOrgChartExportBody.description: What to export an org chart as.

format.description: `pdf`; the document renderer makes PDFs only.

locale.description: `en` or `ar`; the template shows both languages.

SalesPlay.description: A playbook that applies to the deal.

rows_shifted.description: Rows moved now; zero when a job moves them.

manager_id.description: The new manager, or `null` to clear the line.

change_reason.description: Required when the deal is won.

SalesSplitsOutcome.description:
The splits after the change, or the approval a won deal's change waits
on.

force.description: Overwrite even when both sides changed.

deal_lines.description: Both line sets, when both changed.

snapshot_id.description: D6-T8: the snapshot that undoes the sync (30 minutes).

skipped.description: Members left out because their own roles do not allow the access.

partner_contact_ref.description: A partner contact on the team.

user_ref.description: A user on the team; give this or `partner_contact_ref`.

name.description: The new template's name.

id.description: The new draft template.

release.description: The release's CycloneDX 1.5 bill of materials.

target_dir.description:
Absolute path to the directory the three files are written into.
Created if missing. Must resolve inside this checkout's `angular/`.

ScaffoldKind.description:
Which of the two entity pages to generate. `EntityRouteRegistry` keys both
off the same logicalname (`{ formComponent, listComponent }`), so the two
kinds differ only in template, base class, and registry field.

files.description: The `.ts`, `.html`, and `.css` files written, in that order.

registry_note.description:
Why `registry_updated` is false, when it is — the caller has to know
whether to go add the registration by hand.

value.description: The scanned value, exactly as read.

hits.description: Every match, when there was more than one.

status.description: `done`, or `ambiguous` (409) with the records that matched.

ScanHit.description: A record whose scan-enabled field holds the scanned value.

name.description: The record's primary name, when its entity declares one.

ScanLocation.description: Where the device was, when the person lets scans record it.

ScenarioResultRow.description:
`pub` (fields too) — same reason `attome_metric::metric::SnapshotRow` is: `do_evaluate`
below returns these directly, and this crate's own `tests/scenario.rs`
reads their fields straight off the result of a direct call, the same
"call the `pub` `do_*` function, skip the HTTP layer" convention every
other suite in this crate already uses.

affected.description:
Records the rule would refuse, or past runs that would go
differently.

affected_ids.description: The first affected records (rule) or the differing runs (flow).

ScenarioSimulationBody.description: A rule-change or flow-change run for a scenario.

last.description:
`flow_change`: how many of the flow's latest finished runs, 1 to 50
(default 10).

subject_id.description:
The business rule (`rule_change`) or the flow definition
(`flow_change`).

coverage.description: The build's coverage per day (requirement, before, after).

ScheduleDetail.description: A schedule with its assignments and coverage.

quiet_windows.description: `jobs.quiet_windows`, as `{start, end}` in the deployment's time.

ScheduleList.description: The list and the quiet windows heavy schedules wait out.

SchedulePageBody.description:
Full replace, not a partial patch — both fields are always written
exactly as given (`null` clears), so there is no absent-vs-null
ambiguity to resolve (the trap `UpdatePageBody`'s `seo_title`/
`seo_description` sentinel-empty-string convention exists to avoid for a
string field; a plain `Option<DateTime<Utc>>` full-replace is the
simpler fix for a field with no such sentinel).

ScheduledChange.description: T6-T1: one scheduled change of a flag.

SchemaChangeStatus.description:
P-online-schema-change §4(d) — separately polled resource, same reasoning
as `AttributeIndexStatus` above.

status.description: `not_requested | queued | claimed | backfilling | altering | succeeded | failed`.

ScopeRestriction.description: How many records one scope restricted.

ScoreParts.description: How one result came to its score.

fused.description: The fused rank score from the legs, before any tuning.

legs.description: The legs that matched, with the fused statement's per-leg values.

opened.description: Added because the caller opened it from a search lately.

owner.description: Added because the caller owns the record.

pinned.description: Placed by a pin for this query.

score.description: The score shown: `fused + boost_added + owner + opened + team`.

synonyms.description: The synonyms the query also ran with.

team.description: Added because a team of the caller's owns it.

ScreenPop.description: A screen pop: the record a caller's number belongs to.

row_version.description: 0 while the entity has never been set.

attributes.description: Replaces every attribute setting of the entity.

SearchFacets.description:
A25-T9: the results counted by entity, owner (user id) and the month
they last changed (`YYYY-MM`), over every result the caller may see, not
only the page; the most common 20 of each.

oneOf.description: A25-T4: how the score came about, when asked for and allowed.

matched_legs.description:
Which legs matched this row. Useful to a human debugging relevance and
to the impression log's feature vector.

bytes.description: The index table with its indexes, in bytes.

query_norm.description: The normalised query the pin answers.

query.description: The query, as people type it; it is normalised.

oneOf.description: A25-T7: what asking in words did, for `mode=ask`.

degraded.description:
Legs that did not run to completion. **Reported, never swallowed** — a
result set silently missing a leg looks like "no more matches", which
is indistinguishable from a correct empty answer.

oneOf.description: A25-T9: the facets, when asked for.

impression_id.description:
The handle a later interaction is reported against (TODO-021). `None`
when the impression could not be logged, which must not fail the
search.

limited.description:
AB5-T5: the index was down, so this is a short prefix match on each
readable entity's title from the database (route `fallback`), not a
ranked search. Sent only when true.

route.description:
Which route the query took. Exposed deliberately: "why did this query
return that" is the single most common search support question, and the
answer is almost always the route.

oneOf.description:
Set when the query was routed away from retrieval — an aggregation
question, which retrieval answers badly (see `router::Route`).

SearchStatus.description: A25-T5: how far the index is behind, and its size per entity.

sizes.description: Per entity, largest first, from the daily upkeep.

entity_logicalname.description:
For `"entity"`: the entity to route to. For `"saved_search"`: always
`"saved_search"` — pair with `record_id` to call `run`.

terms.description: 2 to 20 terms that mean the same.

SeasonDef.description:
One `calendar_season` row (Z12-T6), identified by `name` within its
calendar. `definition` is an `attome_calendar::rules::Season`.

definition.description:
An `attome_calendar::rules::Season`: `start` and `end` rules and the
hours per weekday between them.

SecretInventoryRow.description: One secret, as an administrator sees it. There is no value field.

active_key_id.description: A key ring's active key id.

active_since.description:
Since when the active key (or the plain secret) has been in use, as
far as the recorded starts show.

key_ids.description: A key ring's key ids; empty for a plain secret.

name.description:
The configuration path, e.g. `auth.jwt_secret` or
`oidc.providers.okta.client_secret`.

rotation.description: `key_ring` (a new key is added beside the old ones) or `replace`.

set.description: Whether this node is configured with it.

webhook_secret_standard.description: M13-T2: the new secret in Standard Webhooks form. Shown once.

oneOf.description:
Optional: the record the user is looking at — a navigation hint,
**never authorization** (I-19, row A-66). Shape-checked only, never
looked up, and stored as one fixed line in the user's message.

session_token.description:
Omit on the very first message of a new conversation. Present on
every subsequent one.

replies.description:
Any new outbound message this call itself produced (a bot ack, a
handoff/offline acknowledgment). Empty when this session was already
handed off to a human — the widget should poll for a human's reply
instead.

session_token.description:
Present on every response — a brand-new value for a first message, the
same value the caller supplied for a resumed one. The widget must
persist this (e.g. `sessionStorage`) and send it back on every later
call.

SendTotals.description: One send's totals over the window.

ok.description: Every record is `ok` (or DKIM is not configured).

message_key.description: The catalog key of the message.

body.description: The stored body; `null` when the site has none (the default applies).

served.description:
What crawlers are served: the body (or the default) with the paths
that are always closed appended.

SeoTopicBody.description: A topic to create or change.

language.description: `en`, `ar`, or a regional form such as `ar-SA`.

SequenceSummary.description: A published sequence, as a rep picks it (D17-T2).

SessionJoined.description: The customer's side of a joined session.

token.description: The customer side's token for its frames.

code.description: Read this to the customer; it works once, for ten minutes.

final_key.description:
Set only once `status = "clean"` — the value the client must PATCH
onto the record's file field. Without this, a polling client would
have no way to learn what the async scan job promoted the object to.

agent_retrieval_mode.description:
The mode the session's agent definition is configured with **now**, for
comparison only: it reaches the next session started from that
definition, never this one. `unrecognised` when the definition holds a
value a new session would refuse to start with; `None` when the session
has no definition or the definition row no longer exists.

allowed_action_ids.description:
The session's effective allow-list, exactly as snapshotted at start.
`None` means "whatever the ceiling permits"; `[]` means nothing — a
supervisor reading the dashboard must see the difference.

capability_pack_refs.description:
D-556 §2 provenance: which capability packs (and which of their
versions) produced the grants above. Never consulted for
authorization; shown so an operator can say where a grant came from.

retrieval_mode.description:
D-561 §5: the knowledge retrieval mode this session **uses** —
`tool_invoked` | `pre_retrieved`, resolved from its agent definition
when it started and stored on the row. Nothing changes it afterwards.

money_cap_minor.description:
Minor units of `currency`; requires the action to declare a money
argument, or every invocation asks first.

row_version.description:
The row's current `row_version` when replacing a row; a stale one is
refused with 409.

time_zone.description: IANA zone for the hours, such as `Asia/Riyadh`; UTC when unset.

undo_seconds.description: Seconds an `act_with_undo` action waits before it runs (30 to 86400).

api_key.description:
The provider's API key. Write-only: no route ever returns it, and the
response carries only its last four characters.

is_set.description:
Q18-T6: a key is stored. The key itself, or any part of it, is never
returned.

updated_at.description: When the stored key was set.

row_version.description: Required to change a flag that exists (409 when stale).

SetEntityAccessItem.description: One entity's levels in a set: 0 None, 1 Team, 2 Business unit, 3 Global.

row_version.description: Required to change a value already set (409 when stale).

can_update.description:
Omitted: true (P-field-write-security, D-141: an admin caller that only
ever sent `can_read` keeps behaving as before, matching the column
default), or false when `mask_format` is set (a masked field cannot be
changed).

mask_format.description:
Q15-T1: show the field only masked: `last4`, `email`, `phone` or
`full`. Needs `can_read`; omitted or null shows it in full.

SetMode.description:
When a `set_value` policy writes: on every write, or on create only when
the field is still empty (after the body, state initial value and
autovalue).

days.description: Days messages are kept, 1 to 3650; none keeps them.

reason.description: Why — shown beside the switch and recorded in the audit event.

SettingDef.description:
One deployment-scope `setting` row (M02/D-412). No `scope`
field — a bundle only ever carries the deployment-scope value for a key,
never an organization- or user-scope override, matching D-412's ruling
that "profile" means "deployment-scope values", nothing more.

key.description:
`"{module}.{name}"` — validated against the live
`SettingRegistry` at apply time once that step exists; export never
writes a key the registry doesn't recognize, since it only ever reads
rows that a registry-checked write already validated.

SettingScope.description:
The scope a stored setting *value* is written at. Resolution order for a
read is always `User -> Organization -> Deployment -> descriptor default`
(M02 §3) — this enum's declaration order matches that precedence.

id.description:
U10-T3: the stored row this value comes from (its audit trail is
`entity_name = "setting"`, `record_id = id`); `null` while the code
default applies, or in a user's own view.

Severity.description:
Severity of an `error` policy. `Error` fails the write (422
`rule_violation`); `Warning` never blocks: the write succeeds and the
warning is returned to the caller (D-791 rule 6) and logged.

ShareLinkSummary.description: One link of a field, as its owner sees it (never the token).

SharedFileUrl.description: What opening a password link answers.

SharedQuery.description: A stored query shared with the caller.

access.description: The most any of the caller's shares allows.

runnable.description: Whether it holds a QuerySpec, so `query/run` can run it by id.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this item: `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer
may update or deactivate it (409 `layer_mismatch` otherwise).

SidebarDef.description:
`sidebar` — one navigation item, addressed by its name path from the
root (`parent_ref` is what the path replaces). `privileges` are the
`sidebar_mm_privilege` rows as privilege keys.

path.description: Root-first name path; the last element is this item's own `name`.

child.description:
The nav tree is one level deep in practice but the type is recursive,
so utoipa needs `no_recursion` to stop expanding it inline — without
it, building the document recurses until the stack overflows. The
emitted schema still carries the `$ref` back to `SidebarItem`, so a
generated client keeps the recursive type.

confirmed_start.description: The Gregorian day the holiday starts, as announced.

SightingRow.description:
One sighted holiday of a Gregorian year: when it is expected to start and,
once confirmed, when it does.

key_id.description: The first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the public key.

signature.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature of the evidence's canonical bytes.

code.description: The emailed code, to sign or decline.

reason.description: Why, to decline.

typed_name.description: The signer's name as they type it, to sign.

chain_row_hash_ok.description:
`None` only while the `DecisionDigest` audit event is pending: still in
`audit_ingest`, not yet chained into `audit_header` (see this
module's doc comment). `false` when the event is missing from both
tables, when more than one digest header exists for the decision, or
when the header row's hash does not recompute.

chain_row_signature_ok.description:
`None` while pending, or when the header row is covered by its chain
batch's signature instead of its own. `false` when the row's signature
does not verify, or when an unsigned row has nothing verifiable
covering it once audit signing is configured.

digest_matches.description:
Recomputed vs. what was stored at decision time. `false` whenever
`digest_recorded` is `false` too (nothing to match against).

digest_recorded.description:
Whether a digest was ever recorded for this decision at all — `false`
for a decision made before this feature existed, or if
`record_decision_digest` failed at decision time (logged, not fatal
to the decide response — see its own doc comment).

recomputed_digest.description: The digest recomputed from this decision's *current* stored state.

verified.description:
`true` only when a digest was recorded, it matches, and the chain row
was checked and checks out clean. Never `true` while the audit
evidence is pending, missing or ambiguous.

captcha_token.description: The CAPTCHA widget's token, when the deployment configures one.

status.description:
`workflow_node_run.status` vocabulary — `succeeded`, `skipped`,
`waiting` (this branch would have suspended for real), or `failed`.

taken_port.description: Set only for `Condition`/`Approval` — which output port fired.

would_have.description:
Human-readable description of the real side effect this node would
have performed outside a dry run — present only for a node whose
live executor has one (D-431: this is the only thing standing in for
it, never the effect itself).

SimulateRecordRef.description: M4-T1: the record a simulation reads.

approval_decisions.description:
`node_id -> "approved" | "rejected"`, consulted by an `Approval` node
reached during the simulated run instead of filing a real
`attome_approval` request. A node with no entry here defaults to
`"approved"` so a simulate run doesn't dead-end at the first
approval gate a caller didn't think to pre-decide.

oneOf.description:
M4-T1: a real record to run the flow against. It is read as the
person simulating (record access and field grants apply) and handed
to the trigger as `{entity, record_id, record}` merged over
`trigger_payload`. Nothing is written.

trigger_payload.description:
Fed to the graph's entry `Trigger` node exactly as a real trigger
