context would be — see `instance_admin::start_instance_internal`'s
`context` for the live equivalent.

status.description:
`completed` (every reachable node settled), `would_wait` (the run hit
a node that would have suspended for real — `WaitForEvent`/
`SubWorkflow`, or a `Wait` past the iteration bound), or `failed`.

Simulation.description: What a check would do to the stored records.

failing_ids.description: The first failing records, in id order.

truncated.description: The preview stopped at its limit before the end of the table.

unknown.description: Records whose condition could not be decided (an evaluation error).

estimated_rows.description: The exact count, or the planner's estimate when it passed.

exact_upto.description: The rows counted, exact up to the threshold plus one.

exceeds.description: Whether the count passed the threshold.

SkipReason.description: Why a member was passed over.

SkippedMember.description: A member passed over on the way, with its reason.

SlaRecalculation.description: The outcome of recalculating one ticket's SLA.

recalculated.description:
`false` when the ticket's SLA was not unresolved (nothing to do), or
its policy no longer exists.

oneOf.description: The ticket's SLA status afterwards; `null` when no SLA was applied.

SloClassStatus.description: One SLO class as an administrator sees it.

budget_remaining.description: The share of the 30-day error budget left (1 = untouched).

error_ratio_30d.description: 5xx responses over all responses in the last 30 days.

oneOf.description: This deployment's own targets, when set.

status.description:
`ok`, `at_risk` or `exhausted` from the error budget; `unmeasured`
for a class without one here.

oneOf.description: The reference targets for this deployment's profile.

SloOverride.description: A deployment's own targets for a class.

profile.description: `solo` or `team`, the profile whose reference targets apply.

report.description:
`{period_start, period_end, latency, classes: [{id, name_en, name_ar,
kind, status, objective, good, bad, error_ratio, budget_remaining}]}`.

row_version.description: Required to change an existing override (409 when stale).

Slot.description: A time that can be booked.

expected_cost.description:
`send` only: the cost the sender agreed to; a larger estimate is
refused.

purpose_key.description: The consent purpose the message is sent under.

cost.description:
`total_segments` at `marketing.sms_price_per_segment`; absent when no
price is set.

recipients.description: People with a phone and SMS consent for the purpose.

dimension_attribute.description:
P9-T5: `None` on the total row; on a member row, the dimension
attribute(s), comma-separated.

dimension_value.description: The member's value (several dimensions' values comma-separated).

children.description:
A section tree nests, so this type is recursive, and utoipa needs
`no_recursion` to stop expanding it inline — without it, building the
workspace OpenAPI document recurses until the stack overflows.
`attome_api::sidebar::SidebarItem::child` carries the identical
annotation for the identical reason; this one was missed, and the
symptom was `server --print-openapi` aborting with 0xC00000FD despite
`main.rs` already spawning a 64 MB stack for exactly this work.

The emitted schema still carries the `$ref` back to `SnapshotSection`,
so a generated client keeps the recursive type.

SnapshotWidget.description:
`pub` (struct and fields) — besides this module's own snapshot
round-trip, `create_from_layout`'s request body and this crate's own
tests construct these directly (see this module's doc comment's
"Write path" section and `do_create_from_layout`, below).

emits.description:
R-07 step 6 — same `#[serde(default)]` reasoning R-02 gave for
`view_id`: a snapshot written before this field existed must still
deserialize. Omitted here, publish/restore/clone silently dropped a
widget's event wiring.

SocialReply.description: A reply to a social message, comment or review.

provider_id.description: The provider's id for the reply, when it gives one.

available.description:
Whether a browser softphone is set up (a Twilio system with an API
key, a TwiML app and the SDK's address).

sdk_url.description: Where the provider's SDK is loaded from (an administrator's setting).

token.description: A Voice SDK access token, valid for an hour.

SourcePosting.description: A source document to post through its rule.

amount.description: A decimal string; negative posts the rule the other way round.

SourceRecord.description: B1-T1: the record an entry's row belongs to.

SpaceTemplatesBody.description: Full-set replace for which templates a space's editors may pick from.

value.description: A scalar; a list for `in`; none for `is_null` and `is_not_null`.

available_after.description: What is left after the spend (negative: over).

SpendLine.description: One money window's month so far.

cap.description: The cap, in the price unit.

forecast.description: Where the window's spend is heading over a whole month.

key.description: The feature id or agent id; empty for the deployment.

percent.description: `spent` as a percentage of `cap` (100 or more: refusing).

spent.description: Spent inside the window, in the price unit.

degrade_at_percent.description: Percent of a cap at which generations are shortened.

model.description: The generation model the prices apply to.

priced.description: Whether that model has a price; without one nothing is counted.

SplitInput.description: One split as a caller gives it.

line_id.description: For a split of one line rather than the whole deal.

dimension_attribute.description: One of the metric's dimension attributes.

period_start.description: The period the targets are for (its start).

shares.description: With `share`: each member's share, summing to 1.

total.description: The parent target.

Stage.description:
A3-T4: how a refusing check (`error`, `required`, `allowed_values`) is
rolled out. `Report` only logs a failure, `Warn` lets the write through
with a warning, `Enforce` refuses it — from `enforce_from` when set, and
as a warning before that date.

drop_off_pct.description:
Percent of records that entered and did not move to the next stage
in order; `null` for the last stage.

stages.description: The stages, in order, as the process document holds them.

allowed_action_ids.description: Optional. Omitted or `null`: whatever the ceiling permits. `[]`: nothing.

mode.description:
Optional (N1-T1): `"develop"` builds — the metadata tools and reads,
so every change is a draft and no record is written; `"run"` acts —
everything but the metadata edit tools. Omitted: no narrowing. It only
narrows `allowed_action_ids`, never widens it.

risk_ceiling.description:
**Required.** `"read"` | `"reversible"` | `"consequential"` — the same
explicit ceiling `POST /agents/{id}/sessions` takes. The agent policy
still bounds it; it never grants anything the caller does not hold.

allowed_action_ids.description: Optional; narrows the agent's own tools further.

max_steps.description:
The most tool steps the run may take (capped by the platform's own
bound); omitted: the platform's bound.

task.description: What the agent is to do.

regarding_entity.description: The record the session is about, if any (a case, a contact).

agent.description:
Optional (V2-D487): a published `agent` metadata object whose tools
become one more allow-list. It only narrows: with
`allowed_action_ids` too, the session gets the actions in both.

allowed_action_ids.description:
Optional. Omitted or `null` means "whatever the ceiling permits"; `[]`
means the session may invoke nothing.

risk_ceiling.description:
**Required.** `"read"` | `"reversible"` | `"consequential"`. There is no
default: the person starting the session states its ceiling. It never
grants anything the caller's own privileges do not already allow.

StateModelDef.description:
M07 Phase 1 (D-405/D-406) — `state_model`, keyed by
`entity_logicalname` (one live model per entity, enforced by a partial
unique index — see `0155_state_lifecycle.sql`).

locked_states.description:
M8-T2: states in which a record is read-only except listed fields.
Omitted from an export when there are none.

reason_field.description: M8-T2: the attribute holding the status reason.

reasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons each state allows.

locked_states.description: M8-T2: states in which a record is read-only except listed fields.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this model.

reason_field.description: M8-T2: the attribute holding the record's status reason.

reasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons each state allows.

record_type.description:
M8-T2: the record type this model governs; absent for the entity's
model of every record without one of its own.

locked_states.description: M8-T2: states in which a record is read-only except listed fields.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this model — `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer may
change or retire it.

reason_field.description: M8-T2: the attribute holding the record's status reason.

reasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons each state allows.

record_type.description:
M8-T2: the record type this model governs; absent for the entity's
model of every record without one of its own.

StateReasons.description: M8-T2: the reasons a record may give for being in `state`.

StateTransitionDef.description:
`state_transition` — set semantics inside its parent
[`StateModelDef`], the same convention [`ProfileField`] uses inside
[`FieldSecurityProfileDef`].

oneOf.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): a `attome-approval` plan the transition runs before
it happens; requires `pending_state`. Omitted from an export when
absent, so bundles without approvals are unchanged.

auto_condition.description:
M8-T3: the condition that makes the transition happen by itself.
Omitted from an export when absent.

guard_expression.description: M45 — nullable, schema-ready, unevaluated in Phase 1.

on_reject_state.description: Where a rejection sends the record; absent means `from_state`.

pending_state.description: The state the record sits in while the approval is open.

amount.description: What it adds to the balance (a payment or credit note is negative).

invoice_id.description: The invoice the line is about.

reference.description:
The document number, the payment's reference, or the write-off's
reason.

language.description: `en` (the default) or `ar`: the language of the emails.

StatusToken.description: A link's token (`?token=`, or the page's form field).

token.description: The signed token from the link.

StepExtras.description: Z10-T2: what a step may add to who decides it and how.

business_hours.description: SLA and reminder minutes count business hours only.

escalate_to.description: Who an escalation goes to (an approver token).

group.description: Consecutive steps with the same group run together, in parallel.

reminder_minutes.description: Remind the approvers this long after the step started waiting.

requires_human.description: A person decides, never an agent.

requires_step_up.description: The decider confirms with a fresh sign-in or second factor.

skip_unless.description: A rules expression; the step runs only when it is true.

risk.description: `Read`, `Reversible` or `Consequential`; absent for an unknown action.

acceptable_factors.description:
The factors the account may answer with (`totp`, `recovery_code`,
`password`, `federated`). `federated` needs the IdP flow, not the
verify route.

StepUpElevationBody.description: The caller's family is elevated until `elevated_until`.

StepUpGoogleBody.description: An answer to a step-up challenge with a fresh Google ID token (BAU-8c).

credential.description: The ID token Google Identity Services just issued. Accepted once.

StepUpStatusBody.description: Whether the caller's own session could perform an operation right now.

acceptable_factors.description:
The factors a step-up for this operation accepts (`totp`,
`recovery_code`, `password`, `federated`), or the single
`totp_enrollment_required`.

elevated.description: Exactly whether the operation's guard passes now.

StepUpVerifyBody.description:
An answer to a step-up challenge. It carries no family and no operation:
those come from the session and the route.

credential.description: The TOTP code, recovery code or password.

StreamEvent.description: One event as the subscriber sees it.

changed_attributes.description:
With `changes` or `record`: the changed attributes the identity may
read.

record.description: With `record`: the record as the identity reads it now.

StreamEventView.description:
One frame's `data`: a stored event, as the stream sends it. The frame's SSE
`id` is `ordinal` and its `event` is `type`.

content.description:
`message.completed` only: the message text, read from the message
ledger when the frame is sent — the event row stores no copy.

ordinal.description: The stream cursor: gapless per conversation.

payload.description: The event's stored payload (references and labels, never content).

type.description: One of the nine semantic event types.

label.description:
A display label derived from the key: the value itself, a lookup
value's target record name when the caller may read it, or the bucket
start in the resolved timezone. `null` for NULL, Total and Other — the
client localizes those.

oneOf.description: `Value`/`Null` only; present when the definition has a series.

series_label.description: The series value's display label, on the same rules as `label`.

values.description:
One value per measure, in definition order. `null` when the measure has
no value for the group (an average over no numeric values).

raw_values.description:
The values before cumulative / percent / moving-average rewrote them,
one row per bucket; absent when nothing was rewritten.

truncated.description: Groups past the limit exist; with `other` they are folded, not dropped.

access_level.description:
The caller's read depth on the entity: `global`, `business_unit`,
`team` or `none` (own and shared records only).

live_rows_only.description: Inactive records never count (`is_active` NULL or true).

StructuredRecords.description:
A drill-through result set: column metadata, rows, the read instant and the
filters that reproduce it, keyset-paged by `next_cursor`. Like
`query/execute`'s tabular shape it is a documented exception to
`CursorPage<T>` (guidelines §12): the metadata around the rows is part of
the contract, so it is not a plain item list.

drill_filters.description:
The definition, binding and bucket predicates as concrete filters, so an
export reproduces exactly these rows. Absent for the Other bucket, whose
NULL-aware complement no filter list can express.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `after_id` for the next page; absent on the last page.

rows.description: One JSON object per record, keyed by column name.

total.description:
Exact: a count over the same scope and drill predicate as the rows,
never an estimate.

reason.description:
M9-T4: why the record is submitted, shown to the approvers (at most
2000 characters).
Why the discount is needed, shown to the approvers.

row_version.description: The request's row version, for a recall.

SubscriptionAsOf.description: A subscription as it stood on a date.

subscription.description: The record as the caller reads it.

SubscriptionCreatedResponse.description:
Same shape as `attome-s2s`'s `KeyCreatedResponse` — the plaintext secret is
returned exactly once, at creation/rotation time, and never again (M62
plan §5: "Secrets never returned by the API after creation, same as S2S
keys").

webhook_secret_standard.description:
M13-T2: the same secret as a Standard Webhooks verifier takes it
(`whsec_…`), for the `webhook-signature` header. Shown once.

external_system.description: L1-T7: the system this subscriber is, for its own external ids.

ordered.description: M13-T3: one record's events are sent one at a time, in order.

paused_at.description: M13-T3: when and why the endpoint's failures turned it off.

target_auth_header.description: M13-T2: the target auth header's name; its value is never returned.

target_url.description:
Never the secret — see `secret_rotate`'s response for the one place a
plaintext secret is ever returned.

reasons.description:
Why it was suggested, for the person: `similar_cases`, `wording` or
`often_used`, strongest first.

reply.description: The reply, rendered for the case and channel.

edit_distance.description:
Required when `outcome = "edited"`, rejected otherwise — migration
`0118`'s CHECK ties the two together in both directions.

outcome.description:
`accepted` | `edited` | `rejected`. There is deliberately no `pending`:
a decision cannot move a row back to undecided, which is what keeps an
abandoned suggestion distinguishable from a rejected one.

recorded.description:
`false` when this decision was not the first one recorded. A
double-submit from the UI must not overwrite an accept with a reject,
so the first decision wins and the caller is told which theirs was.

SurfaceSwitchView.description: One surface as the admin screen shows it.

configured.description:
What the deployment's configuration allows. Changing it takes a
restart; this route never does.

effective.description: `configured AND runtime_enabled`, as the gate applies it.

runtime_enabled.description:
The runtime switch: `false` only when an administrator turned it off.
`null` when the switch state could not be read — which every AI
surface treats as off.

SurveyForm.description: A survey as the respondent sees it.

questions.description: The questions: key, label, label_ar, type, required, options.

token.description: The signed token from the email.

config.description: L1-T3: a `source_system_rank` rule's trust per system per attribute.

waiting_because.description: Why it waits, when it does.

SwitchoverApproval.description: The approval a switchover waits on.

candidate.description: The member to promote; Patroni picks one when absent.

reason.description: Why, for the approver and the audit trail (10 to 500 characters).

SyncLine.description: One line as the hash sees it.

SyncOutcome.description:
The result of one [`sync`] call. `approval_pending` mirrors
`routes::ApplyAccepted`'s field of the same name/meaning byte for byte —
deliberately, so `bundle-tool`'s `render::approval_request_id` (written
against `ApplyAccepted`'s shape) recognizes this reply too with no
special-casing.

credential_configured.description:
Whether `credential_value` was provided and stored — never the value
itself.

SystemStatus.description: What a signed-in person should know about the system right now.

read_only.description: Changes are refused for now (the audit backlog guard is holding writes).

read_only_reason.description: AB5-T6: `operator`, `disk` or `recovery` while read-only mode is on.

dead_ratio.description: Dead rows over all rows; 0 for an empty table.

growth_rows_7d.description: Live rows added over the last seven days, when a sample exists.

lookups_without_index.description: Lookup fields no index leads on.

unused_indexes.description:
Indexes never scanned since statistics were reset (unique and primary
keys excepted: they enforce rules even unscanned).

TagMergeResult.description: What a merge or its undo did.

dropped.description:
Links dropped because the record already carried the other tag (a
merge only; an undo cannot bring these back).

moved.description: Links moved to the other tag.

TagSuggestion.description: A suggestion: the tag and how many records carry it.

TagView.description: One tag as the caller sees it.

TaggedRecord.description: One record carrying a tag, as the caller may see it.

allow_host.description:
K6-T1: the one intranet host this source may reach (K6-T8); empty
keeps every private address refused.

audience.description: K6-T1: `internal | partner | customer` — who may read what it imports.

credential_ref.description: K6-T1: reference to the credential the crawl signs in with.

exclude_patterns.description: K6-T1: path patterns to skip, one glob per line.

include_patterns.description: K6-T1: path patterns to crawl, one glob per line (empty: everything).

languages.description: K6-T1: `ar` and/or `en`; empty keeps every language.

watch_only.description: K6-T1: watch for changes and report them, import nothing.

TeamAccess.description: The access a member gets to the deal.

TestAudience.description:
Who the rule is tested for. Absent: the rule is evaluated as if it
applied, every policy included.

interactive.description:
`false` for an API-key or S2S principal, which skips locks (D-791
rule 3). Default `true`.

system.description:
A system context (workflow, bundle record sets): no locks, no
role-scoped rules.

scope_ref.description: The app, unit, domain (host name) or portal; empty for the deployment.

ThemeRow.description: One version of a scope's theme.

ThemeTokens.description: A theme: every token optional, so a scope overrides only what it sets.

app_name.description:
The product name shown in emails and the browser, such as "Acme CRM"
(at most 60 characters).

TimelineEntry.description: One entry in a record's timeline.

actor.description: B1-T1: who acted — the user, or the user an agent or flow acted for.

actor_kind.description: B1-T1: what kind of actor made the entry.

detail.description:
Kind-specific detail (audit operation and readable changed fields,
communication subject/channel, note title, activity type, decision
status, approval action and status, flow name, agent actions, …). A
JSON object rather than one struct with mostly-empty fields across
unrelated shapes.

pinned.description: B1-T2: pinned on this record, shown above the rest.

run_id.description: B1-T1: the agent session or flow instance, when the entry came from one.

source_entity.description:
The entity or ledger table the underlying row belongs to —
`audit_header`, `audit_detail` (state transitions),
`communication`, `note`, `activity`, `dashboard_decision`,
`approval_request`, `workflow_instance` or `agent_session`.

source_record.description:
B1-T1: the record the underlying row belongs to: this record, or a
related record rolled in.

summary.description: Short, human-readable description of the event.

TimelineEntryKind.description:
The source an entry came from. Entries sort by their wire name within one
timestamp, so the order is stable and documented: `activity`,
`agent_run`, `approval`, `audit_event`, `communication`, `decision`,
`flow_run`, `note`, `state_transition`.

ToKind.description: Who a ticket is handed to.

TokenChange.description: One token that differs between a version and its scope's published one.

assertion.description: S11-T2: the identity provider's token (jwt-bearer grant).

grant_type.description:
`client_credentials`, or `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`
with a token from a trusted identity provider in `assertion`.

scope.description: Space-separated scopes; omit for every scope the client holds.

ToolCallCounts.description: One action's tool-call events in the window.

by_action.description: One row per action id, sorted by it.

ToolCallView.description:
A persisted tool call, for display. An allow-list of columns: the stored
`outcome`, leases, gate decisions and row versions are not exposed.
`arguments` is **display only** — a confirmation sends back
`arguments_hash` and nothing else (I-13, row A-08).

oneOf.description: The match set was bounded, so this is the real number.

The match set hit the candidate ceiling. There are at least this many;
counting the rest would cost a second full-predicate pass.

TourView.description: One guided tour as a signed-in person receives it (B14-T1).

auto_start.description: Starts by itself the first time the person opens `route`.

route.description: The app path prefix the tour belongs to.

TraceStep.description: One step of a session's run, in order (N29-T2).

tool_call_id.description: The tool call that asked for it, when an agent did.

Tracked.description: A shipment's status after a tracking read.

changed.description: Whether this read moved the shipment.

last_event_key.description: The carrier's latest update code, when it has one.

segments.description: `[{start, end, text}]`, seconds from the start.

oneOf.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): when set, asking for this transition moves the
record to `pending_state` and opens a `attome-approval` request running
this plan; approval moves it to `to_state`. Omitted when absent.

auto_condition.description:
M8-T3: the condition that makes the transition happen by itself.
Omitted when absent.

guard_expression.description:
M45 attome-rules expression, evaluated on every write path with the
record's fields and `current_user`; fail closed.

on_reject_state.description: Where a rejection sends the record; absent means `from_state`.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this transition (it may differ
from its model's: a project may add a transition to a platform model).

pending_state.description: The state the record sits in while the approval is open.

TransitionRequestBody.description:
`POST /api/v1/{entity}/{id}/transition` — a state change by target state.
Runs the generic record update path (identical to a `PATCH` of the state
field, M07 §4.1); `comment` is recorded on the audit event. No
`row_version` in the body: send `If-Match` for optimistic concurrency, or
omit it to transition from the record's current version.

approval_request_id.description:
M07 Phase F (D-770): present only when the requested transition
requires approval. The record is parked in `to_state` (the pending
state) and this request decides it; approval moves the record to
`requested_state`. Omitted otherwise.

requested_state.description:
The state that was asked for, when an approval now stands between the
record and it. Omitted otherwise.

to_state.description:
The state the record is in now. For a transition that requires
approval (M07 Phase F) this is the transition's pending state, not the
one asked for — see `approval_request_id`.

source_version.description: The source's latest published version; none when never published.

stale.description: The source has a newer published version than that.

translated_from_version.description: The source version this translation was last brought up to date with.

edge_types.description:
Restricts which edges the walk follows — `"lookup:{field}"`,
`"hierarchy:{field}"`, `"relationship:{type}"`, or the bare
`"relationship"` to admit every relationship type. `None` (the
default) follows everything the caller can see.

truncated.description:
Set whenever a bound (depth, per-hop fan-out, the overall node cap, or
the statement timeout) cut the walk short. Never silently return a
partial graph.

TreeComputed.description: One metric of a tree computation.

outcome.description: `computed`, `skipped` (a snapshot for the period existed) or `failed`.

TreeRecord.description:
One row of the draft tree, in the same `{id, row_version, data}` shape the
generic entity list returns, so the editor can keep sending `If-Match`
updates through generic CRUD with the `row_version` it read here.

entities.description: Populated only at the root (no query params).

files.description:
Files whose `folder` matches exactly — only when `folder` is given
(there is no such thing as a folder-less document, so this is always
empty at the record level without a `folder` param).

folders.description:
Populated once `entity_name` + `record_id` are both given — the
subfolders directly under `folder` (root of the record's document
space when `folder` is omitted).

records.description: Populated only when `entity_name` is given without `record_id`.

addressed_item_ref.description:
The Knowledge Base item that answers this gap. Written only when
`status = "addressed"`; ignored otherwise.

TrialBalanceRow.description: One account's totals in a trial balance.

agreement.description: same / (same + different); `null` before anything was compared.

different_sample.description: The latest decisions a person did differently (at most 50).

attempts.description: Failed dispatch attempts that were counted.

last_error.description: The last counted failure, as the dispatcher logged it.

operation.description: `create`, `update`, … as written to the change feed.

dispatched.description:
Workflow instances this replay newly started; 0 when every trigger
the event matches had already started. Waits are never resumed.

reason.description: The departure, e.g. `automatic: volume: observed 200, expected 5`.

email.description:
Masked (`z***@example.com`): the owner recognises it; the caller
never needs the address itself.

pending_email.description: Masked: the address a link sent but not yet opened would add.

client_ip.description:
The player's address as the calling server saw it on its own
connection. Used for rate limits and the audit trail.

code.description:
D-780: for an account with MFA, the player's TOTP code or one of their
recovery codes (without it such an account answers `mfa_required`).

create_if_missing.description: Create the account when `login` is a free, valid username.

auth_epoch.description:
The credential epoch: sessions the caller issued under an older
epoch are revoked (password change, disable, log out everywhere).

outcome.description:
`ok`, `created`, `bad_credentials`, `name_rejected`,
`password_rejected`, `disabled`, `rate_limited`, `mfa_required` or
`mfa_failed` (D-780: the code was wrong, replayed or used up).

reason.description: For `name_rejected` and `password_rejected`: why, for the player.

recovery_code_used.description:
D-780: `ok` with a recovery code (one fewer left; the owner is told by
email when the account has one).

retry_after_secs.description: For `rate_limited`: seconds until trying again helps.

username.description: The account's username (case as stored), for `ok` and `created`.

TurnCount.description: How many turns ended one way in the last day.

citations.description: The turn's executed knowledge actions' citations (row A-56).

model_id.description: The model that wrote `text`, when one did.

terminal_state.description: One of the twelve terminal states (D-565).

awaiting.description:
Ended with `awaiting_confirmation` or `awaiting_approval`: stopped for
a human, neither a success nor a failure.

cancelled.description:
Ended with `cancelled`: the user pressed Stop (C11 B4). Neither a
success nor a failure, so counted on its own.

ended.description: `turn.completed` events in the window. Each turn ends exactly once.

failed.description: Ended with any of the other nine states.

key.description: The built-in text's catalogue key, e.g. `xrmForm.save`.

text.description: What to show instead, at most 500 characters.

UiTextOverrides.description: This deployment's rewordings of built-in interface text in one language.

texts.description: Catalogue key (`xrmForm.save`) to the text shown instead.

UnauthorizedResponse.description:
A 401 from a route guarded by a step-up (D-510): either the standard
envelope (`unauthorized`, for a missing session or a session without a live
refresh family) or a [`ReauthRequiredResponse`]. Clients tell them apart by
`error`. Documentation-only.

UndoItem.description:
B5-T3: one record's values before a bulk edit, and the row version the
edit leaves it at.

row_version.description:
The record's row version once the edit has applied; an undo only
reverts a record still at it.

values.description: The changed attributes' values before the edit.

UndoItemView.description: One item of an undo run.

UndoRunView.description: An undo run and a page of its items.

summary.description: Item counts by outcome, once finished.

UnresolvedReason.description:
Why a ticket's SLA has no deadline (D-517) — the value stored in
`service_ticket.sla_unresolved_reason`.

UnresolvedRecalculationSummary.description: A bounded page of unresolved-SLA recalculation.

next_after.description: Pass back as `after` for the next page; `null` when this was the last.

skipped.description:
Skipped because a concurrent pause/resume held the ticket's clock
lock; they stay unresolved and a later page run picks them up.

can_act_as_user.description: S1-T10: grant or withdraw acting as a user.

expires_at.description: S11-T4: a new expiry (in the future); the owner is reminded again.

oauth_public_key_pem.description:
S11-T1: the PEM public key (RSA, P-256/P-384 or Ed25519) that checks
the client's token-endpoint assertions; an empty string removes it.

oauth_scopes.description: S11-T1: the scopes an access token may carry.

service_user_ref.description:
Re-point the client at a different `user_account`, or set one on
a client created before the field was required (such a client is
rejected by `s2s_authn` until this is set). Omit to keep the current
value; it cannot be cleared.

description.description:
Absent = leave unchanged; empty string clears the description back to
`NULL` (same convention as that handler's `category` field).

name.description:
Absent = leave unchanged (same convention as
`admin::entity::update_entity`'s `UpdateEntityBody`).

row_version.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard (guidelines §2).

steward_ref.description:
Absent = leave unchanged. There is deliberately no way to explicitly
clear an already-set steward/deputy back to unassigned in this pass
— reassign to a different systemuser, or delete and recreate the
domain, until a real need for clearing is demonstrated.

UpdateDrillSchedule.description: A schedule change; absent fields stay as they are.

business_key.description:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (D-787 rule 7): declare the business key — 1 to 4
field logical names, in order (text, number, date, bool or lookup;
single-valued; a lookup's target must itself have a key). An empty
list clears it; absent leaves it unchanged. Refused with 409
`business_key_duplicates` while live records share a key value.

category.description: Set to an empty string to clear the category back to uncategorized.

is_reference_data.description:
Mark the entity as reference data (requires a business key):
generic writes to it are recorded as `upsert_record` when a changeset
is in play. Absent leaves it unchanged.

oneOf.description:
L1-T1: the entity's master-data settings, written as one
`set_entity_master_data` changeset operation. `is_master: true`
needs the entity to be in a data domain (422 naming `is_master`).
Absent leaves them unchanged.

UpdateIssueBody.description: A status change of one issue.

accepted_reason.description: Why the issue is accepted as it is; required for `accepted`.

scan_schedule.description: A15-T6: `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, or `""` to scan on demand only.

UpdatePageBody.description:
The optimistic-concurrency guard is the `If-Match` header (D-079's
contract, reused as-is), not a body field — `attome-api`'s
`content_admin::update_page` parses it before this deserializes.

UpdatePermissionSetBody.description:
Fields left out stay as they are; the name is the set's key and does not
change.

UpdateRecoveryTarget.description: A target's new numbers; absent ones stay.

UpdateRoleBody.description:
`name`/`description` only — `position_hierarchy_enabled` has its own
dedicated endpoint (`PUT .../roles/{id}/position-hierarchy`,
`role_entity_access.rs`) because toggling it must invalidate every
current holder's cached `SecurityContext` (it changes `resolve()`'s
output, unlike a role's display name/description); folding it into this
generic PATCH would make that invalidation easy to forget on a future
edit to this handler.

description.description: Set to an empty string to clear the description.

ip_allowlist.description:
Omit to leave the current allow-list untouched; `[]` clears it back
to unrestricted. Validated the same way `create_role` validates it —
see `CreateRoleBody::ip_allowlist`'s doc comment.

row_version.description: The version the change was made against.

description.description:
`None` leaves the stored value unchanged, `Some("")` clears it,
`Some(nonempty)` sets it — same convention as `UpdatePageBody`'s
`seo_title`/`seo_description`.

UpdateStateModelBody.description:
Full replacement of the model's mutable fields (`entity_logicalname` is
the immutable identity, same posture as an entity's own `logicalname`).

locked_states.description: M8-T2: full replacement, like every field here.

external_system.description: L1-T7: omitting it keeps the current one; an empty one removes it.

filter_entity_logicalnames.description:
Omitting the field keeps the current filter; providing one (`[]` for
"match nothing" or a non-empty list) replaces it wholesale. Phase 1
has no way to PATCH a filter back to NULL ("match everything") short
of deleting and recreating the subscription — a narrower surface than
double-`Option` JSON semantics would give, deliberately: serde's
default `Option<Option<T>>` handling cannot distinguish an absent key
from an explicit `null` without a custom deserializer this crate
doesn't carry, and a silently-wrong distinction here is worse than a
missing feature.

filter_event_names.description:
Same replace-wholesale-or-omit convention as the two filters above —
see this struct's doc comment. Migration `0441`.

ordered.description: M13-T3: omitting it keeps the current one.

payload_shape.description: M13-T1: `id`, `changes` or `full`; omitting it keeps the current one.

target_auth_header.description:
M13-T2: replaces the target's auth header (name and value together);
an empty name removes it; omitting both keeps it.

UpdateTransitionBody.description:
Full replacement of the transition's mutable fields + optimistic
concurrency, same shape as `UpdateStateModelBody`. `from_state`/`to_state`
are optional: omitted keeps the edge's current end, present moves it —
validated exactly as on create (an option of the model's state field; a
second live edge with the same `(from, to)` is `409`).

oneOf.description:
Full replacement like every other field here: omitted clears the
approval (the transition happens on write again). See
`CreateTransitionBody::approval_plan`.

auto_condition.description:
Full replacement: omitted makes the transition a manual one again.
See `CreateTransitionBody::auto_condition`.

safety_point.description: The backup or snapshot the upgrade can go back to.

contract_applied_at.description: When the contract step (the old schema's removal) ran.

verification_evidence_id.description: The signed evidence of the verification (AB4-T2).

entity.description:
Entity logicalname, resolved to `entity_info.id` server-side
(`resolve_entity_ref`) — never a client-supplied UUID, same
convention `shares::create_record_share`/`shares::create_entity_default_share`
use.

read_access_level.description:
Each defaults to `Global` (3) on a brand-new grant row — matching
`role_mm_entity_access`'s own DB column default, so creating a
grant that only narrows (say) `delete_access_level` doesn't silently
narrow read/write too.

read_owner_visible.description:
D-371: each defaults to `false` — matching the DB column default, so
upserting a grant that only narrows a depth doesn't silently opt the
role into owner-visibility too.

UsageIn.description: One usage record as the sender reports it.

idempotency_key.description: The sender's key for this record; repeating it is harmless.

metric.description: What was used, such as `api_calls` or `storage_gb_hours`.

UsageResponse.description:
U11-T1: what this deployment runs and who uses it. There are no seats or
expiry dates in v2 (D-778); this is information, not enforcement.

users_signed_in_30d.description: Accounts that signed in during the last 30 days.

record_row_version.description:
The record's `row_version` the caller saw (record conflicts; the write
is refused with 409 when the record changed since).

config.description: The raw `dashboard_widget.config` payload a client is about to save.

widget_type.description:
The widget type the config is for. Omitted means `declarative_widget`,
this route's original contract. For any other type the route checks
that the type is renderable and validates `config.data` (a structured
definition) and `config.bindings` (dashboard 10/10 Phase 2.1).

entity.description: The entity's logical name; its fields are the expression's fields.

sample_record_id.description:
A record of `entity` to evaluate the expression on; the response then
carries its value and evaluation trace. The record is read as the
caller.

doc.description: The document to check, as it would be saved.

since.description: The start of the rejection window.

public_key.description: The application server key for `PushManager.subscribe`, base64url.

cycle_time.description:
`{"per_case": {...}, "per_step": {...}}` — cycle-time percentiles;
carried alongside variants rather than exposed as a third route,
since both read from the same snapshot row and the module plan's
Phase 1 checklist does not call for a dedicated cycle-time endpoint.

from.description: The version current before; `null` when none was.

to.description:
The version current now. Every node switches to it on its next
metadata catch-up.

ViewDef.description:
`view` — one view. `entity_logical_name` (a uuid despite its
name) is carried as the entity's logicalname; `sql_query_ref` as the
query's logical key.

kind.description:
D-429 — `list` (default) | `kanban` | `calendar` | `timeline`. Only
`system`-scope views are ever bundle-exported/reconciled; `personal`/
`shared` rows are per-user runtime data.

view_metadata.description:
D-429 — kind-specific settings (`state_field`/`wip_limits` for
kanban; `start_field`/`end_field`/`color_field` for calendar/timeline).

kind.description:
D-429 (+ chart, migration 0447) — how this view renders: `list`
(default), `kanban`, `calendar`, `timeline`, `chart`. Kind-specific
settings live in `view_metadata`.

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785) — the layer that owns this view: `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer
may update or retire a system view (409 `layer_mismatch` otherwise).
Personal and shared views are user data and always `project`.

scope.description:
D-429 — always `system` through this admin surface; `personal`/
`shared` views are created and promoted only through the self-service
`/api/v1/views` routes below.

view_metadata.description:
D-429 — kind-specific settings, advisory only. Never a source of
server-side enforcement: a kanban `state_field`/`wip_limits` never
substitutes for `attome-state`'s own transition checks, a
calendar/timeline `start_field`/`end_field` never substitutes for the
view's own privilege/record-security gate, and a chart's
`x_field`/`y_fields`/aggregation never substitutes for `query/execute`
actually returning that column (see `chart_view_metadata`'s doc
comment).

ViewImpact.description: What editing or removing a view would touch (A13-T6).

dashboard_widgets.description: Dashboard widgets that show it, and the dashboards they are on.

is_default.description: Every user's default list for this entity.

owner_layer.description: The layer that owns it; a `platform` view is built in.

sidebar_items.description: Navigation entries whose route names it.

warnings.description: What to tell the person about to change it.

heartbeat_secs.description: Seconds until the next heartbeat is due.

viewers.description: Everyone else viewing the record now, most recent first.

VisitorFrame.description: A customer frame, with the side's token.

VoicemailRequest.description: A voicemail to drop into a call.

Vote.description: Up or down, and nothing else.

VoteAck.description:
A "was this useful" body-less struct wrapper isn't needed: `VoteBody`
(`attome-content::model`) already carries `url_path` + `useful`. Same
D-367 posture as `view_page` — identical 404 whether the page doesn't
exist, isn't published, or Content Management isn't licensed.

VoteBody.description:
The public/anonymous-safe "was this useful" vote body (D-452). Identifies
the page by `url_path`, the same identifier `content_public.rs`'s
`/content/view` already resolves by — a caller who can see a page can
always vote on it without needing its internal id.

Warehouse.description: The warehouse a script is for.

schema_version.description: The export's schema version the script was written for.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

confirm.description: Must be `true`: the person has seen the preview.

avg_csat.description:
Average `service_ticket.csat_score` across every ticket whose `channel`
is `web_chat` (M76's existing CSAT-on-close convention — reused
verbatim, no new scoring mechanism). `NULL` until an agent has both
converted a web-chat work request into a ticket (M70) and closed it
with a score.

avg_first_response_seconds.description:
Average time, in seconds, between a conversation's first inbound
message and its first outbound reply (bot ack, offline message, or
handoff ack) — `NULL` until at least one conversation has both.

conversations_last_30_days.description:
Distinct conversations started (`communication` rows with
`channel = 'web_chat', direction = 'inbound', in_reply_to IS NULL`)
in the last 30 days.

WebVital.description: AA12-T1: one Web Vitals measurement from a browser.

area.description: The screen's first path segment (e.g. `xrm`, `admin`), for grouping.

name.description: `LCP` (largest contentful paint) or `INP` (interaction to next paint).

new.description: Of those, new ones (the rest were delivered before).

WebhookPayload.description:
S2-T12: the body of every outbound webhook delivery, published as the
`WebhookPayload` schema under the document's `webhooks.entityChanged`.
An audit-stream subscription sends the same shape with `entity`
`audit_header` and the audit event as `data`.

changed_attributes.description:
M13-T1: the attributes the write changed that the owner may read, on
`changes` and `full` shapes; `null` on `id`, when the owner cannot
read the record, or when the source did not record them.

changes.description:
M13-T1, `changes` shape only: `{attribute: {old, new}}` for each
changed attribute the owner may read; a sensitive value is
`{"ref": true}`.

data.description:
The record as the subscription's owner may read it now, or `null`
when they cannot read it or it is gone. `full` shape only.

entity.description: The changed record's entity logical name.

event_id.description:
The event's id; also the `Idempotency-Key` header, the same on every
retry of one event.

event_name.description:
M13-T1: the named business event (`sla.breached`, `record.merged`),
or `null` for an ordinary entity change.

occurred_at.description: When the change was matched to the subscription.

operation.description: `create`, `update`, `delete`, and the other entity change operations.

headcount_delta.description: Agents added to (or, negative, taken from) every interval.

service_level.description:
Service level per interval in percent (live channels; absent for
deferred work or an interval with no volume).

WidgetCitation.description:
A citation as an anonymous visitor may see it (C11 B6, row A-86): the
article's title and the section cited — never a record, collection or
chunk id, and no link, because a knowledge article has no public address.

heading_path.description: The cited section's heading path, outermost first.

applied_filters.description: Every filter the number was computed with, and where each came from.

definition_fingerprint.description: Stable for identical definitions and inputs.

deprecated_alias_of.description:
D-479 (M26 R-09) — set when `type_id` is a legacy id kept only so an
already-migrated `dashboard_widget.widget_type` value (written by
the now-deleted legacy dashboard-migration job, D-790) still resolves
to a real descriptor.
Names the modern `type_id` a viewer should actually render this
widget with — the palette/builder should offer the modern id, not
this one, for a brand-new widget. `None` for every non-legacy
descriptor.

render_kind.description:
D-525 — filled in by [`WidgetRegistry::register`] from the renderer
table (an alias inherits its target's), so no descriptor can claim a
renderer the viewer does not have.

schema.description:
Descriptive only — see this module's doc comment for why no schema
enforcement exists yet.

type_id.description:
Matches one value in `dashboard_widget.widget_type`'s choice list
(`seed.rs`) — the two must stay in sync, which is why `seed.rs` reads
its choice list from [`WidgetRegistry::type_ids`] rather than
duplicating this table.

WidgetInputs.description: What a viewer may send to a data route: values, never definitions.

cross_filters.description:
Cross-filter variable values by name. Only variables the widget listens
to apply; the rest are ignored, so one page-wide map serves every widget.

page_size.description: Row page size for a query-backed (Class C) widget, 1–200.

parameters.description:
Values for declared dashboard parameters, by name. A `date_range`
parameter takes `{ "start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "end": "YYYY-MM-DD" }`; every
other type takes a string (a number may also be a JSON number). `null`
or an omitted name falls back to the declared default.

preview.description:
Execute the editor's draft instead of the published version. Needs
record Update on the dashboard; without it the dashboard reads as
missing (404).

WidgetRecordsInputs.description:
What a viewer may send to the records route: the data route's values plus
which bucket to list.

after_id.description: Keyset cursor: the `next_cursor` of the previous page.

oneOf.description:
A bucket key exactly as the data route returned it; omitted lists every
row the (ungrouped) number covers.

applied_filters.description: The same filters the number was computed with, and their origins.

definition_fingerprint.description: Equal to the data route's fingerprint for the same inputs.

channel.description:
E27-T1: the channel the consent is for (`any` when absent): `email`,
`sms`, `whatsapp`, `phone` or `ads`.

WorkItemRollupRow.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/project/{id}/work-items/rollup` — a work item's
own stored fields plus its point rollup. The client builds the WBS tree
from `parent_work_item_id`, the same flat-list-plus-parent-pointer shape
`entity/document-folder/document-folder-browser.component.ts` already
renders recursively.

is_critical_path.description:
Critical Path Method result — see `critical_path.rs` for the
algorithm and its documented scope (`finish_to_start` dependencies
only). `false`/`None` (not an error) when the project's dependency
graph has a cycle, or when this item isn't part of the dependency
network at all (an isolated item's float is trivially `0`, so it IS
still marked critical — only a genuine cycle degrades to `None`).

points_completed.description:
Sum of `points` over every leaf *descendant* of this node (itself,
if this node is a leaf).

points_own.description:
This node's own `points` value — meaningful only when it is itself a
leaf (`points_total == points_own` in that case); 0 for a
phase/parent row regardless of what its `points` column happens to
hold, per the "parent tasks and phases do not carry their own
progress" rule.

progress_pct.description:
`points_completed / points_total * 100`; `0.0` when `points_total`
is `0` (no leaf descendants yet, e.g. an empty phase).

WorkbenchRow.description: A20-T1/T3: where one label-able text stands in a language.

status.description:
`untranslated`, `stale` (the source changed since it was translated),
`draft` (not yet reviewed) or `reviewed`.

WorkflowMovePreview.description: What moving the run would do.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

post.description: Sent to a subscription's `target_url` for each matching change. Any 2xx answer ends the delivery. Any other status, a connection failure, or no answer within 15 seconds is retried: the wait starts at 10 seconds and doubles up to 15 minutes, until the subscription's `max_attempts` (8 for the `standard` retry class, 20 for `extended`, at most 25), after which the delivery is dead-lettered and can be replayed by an administrator. A target the SSRF guard rejects at send time is dead-lettered at once. Retries carry the same `Idempotency-Key`, so drop a key you have already handled.

parameters.description: `t=<unix ms>,v1=<hex>`: HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the subscription's secret (hex-decoded), over `<t>.<raw body>`. Recompute it over the exact bytes received, compare in constant time, and reject a `t` far from your clock. Header: `X-Attome-Signature`.
parameters.name: X-Attome-Signature

parameters.description: The event id, the same on every retry of one event.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

default.description: Anything else is retried, as described above.
